games: Cookie Clicker (Orteil). Read from the live source main.js, fetched 2026-10-12 from https://orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js; the line numbers below refer to that copy. Cross-checked against the Cookie Clicker wiki (https://cookieclicker.fandom.com/wiki/Golden_Cookie), which was read through its api.php wikitext endpoint because the normal page returns HTTP 402.

AdVenture Capitalist (Hyper Hippo / Kongregate). Read from the AdCap wiki pages Businesses, Angel_Investors, Unlocks_(Earth), Cash_Upgrades and Managers, also through api.php wikitext. Checked against Anthony Pecorella's 'The Math of Idle Games' Parts I-III (gamedeveloper.com) and a Steam thread that lists the angel thresholds.
Realm Grinder and Egg, Inc. Prestige formulas only, quoted in Pecorella Part III (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/the-math-of-idle-games-part-iii).

curves.name: Building price (geometric 1.15 per owned)
curves.formula: price = ceil( basePrice * 1.15^max(0, owned - free) * priceModifiers ). Buying n more costs the sum over i = owned .. owned+n-1 of basePrice*1.15^i. Selling n refunds that sum times 0.25.
curves.parameters: Game.priceIncrease = 1.15 (line 7972). Sell multiplier giveBack = 0.25 (line 8119); the Earth Shatterer aura raises it toward 0.5. 'free' buildings do not raise the price. Price doubles every ln2/ln1.15 = 4.96 purchases.
curves.purpose: Each building's cost grows geometrically while its output grows linearly, which produces the buy-wait seesaw. The 25% refund lets a player undo a bad buy at a loss.

curves.name: Building base price and base CpS by tier index n
curves.formula: For n >= 1: baseCps = round_to_2_sig( ceil(n^(0.5n + 2) * 10) / 10 ). basePrice = round_to_2_sig( (n + 9 + (n<5 ? 0 : 5*(n-5)^1.75)) * 10^n * max(1, n-14) ), then x10 if n>=16, another x10 if n>=17, another x10 if n>=18, and x20 if n>=19. The Cursor (n=0) is hand-set: price 15, CpS 0.1.
curves.parameters: Computed values (price / CpS / base payback in seconds): Cursor 15/0.1/150; Grandma 100/1/100; Farm 1,100/8/138; Mine 12,000/47/255; Factory 130,000/260/500; Bank 1.4e6/1,400/1,000; Temple 2e7/7,800/2,564; Wizard tower 3.3e8/44,000/7,500; Shipment 5.1e9/2.6e5/19,615; Alchemy lab 7.5e10/1.6e6/46,875; Portal 1e12/1e7/1e5; Time machine 1.4e13/6.5e7; Antimatter condenser 1.7e14/4.3e8; Prism 2.1e15/2.9e9; Chancemaker 2.6e16/2.1e10; Fractal engine 3.1e17/1.5e11; Javascript console 7.1e19/1.1e12; Idleverse 1.2e22/8.3e12; Cortex baker 1.9e24/6.4e13; You 5.4e26/5.1e14. From tier to tier, price rises about x11-16 and CpS about x5.4-8, so base payback roughly doubles each tier.
curves.purpose: One closed-form formula sets the whole generator ladder, so the designer tunes two exponents instead of 20 rows. Each newer tier is better per building but worse per cookie spent.
curves.source: https://orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js lines 8012-8035 (Game.Object constructor) and 8979 onward (building definitions). The table was computed by running that formula.

curves.name: Tiered building upgrades (x2 per tier)
curves.formula: Each owned tiered upgrade for a building multiplies that building's CpS by 2 (GetTieredCpsMult; 'unshackled' upgrades raise this later). Upgrade price = building basePrice * tierPrice.
curves.parameters: Owned count that unlocks each tier, with its price factor: 1 (x10), 5 (x50), 25 (x500), 50 (x50,000), 100 (x5e6), 150 (x5e8), 200 (x5e11), 250 (x5e14), 300 (x5e17), 350 (x5e20), 400 (x5e24), 450 (x5e28), 500 (x5e32), 550 (x5e36), 600 (x5e40). Synergy upgrades unlock at 15 and 75 of two buildings.
curves.purpose: Milestone doublings at 1, 5, 25, 50, 100, then every 50, which push back against the 1.15 cost growth.

curves.name: Cookies per click
curves.formula: perClick = mult * ( 1 * 2^(number owned of {Reinforced index finger, Carpal tunnel prevention cream, Ambidextrous}) + add ). add = 0.1 * (non-cursor buildings owned) * fingerMults + 0.01 * CpS for each mouse upgrade owned. A Cursor building produces (0.1 * 2^same + add) * mult per second.
curves.parameters: The three click doublers cost 100, 500 and 10,000 cookies. Thousand fingers costs 100,000 and adds +0.1 per non-cursor building. Million fingers multiplies that by 5, Billion by 10, and each later tier by 20. Each mouse upgrade (Plastic mouse costs 50,000) adds 1% of CpS to each click.
curves.purpose: Clicking starts as the only source and stays relevant late in the game because click value is tied to building count and to a percentage of CpS.

curves.name: Golden cookie spawn timer
curves.formula: Each frame (30 fps) with no golden cookie on screen: time++, and a cookie spawns with probability ((time - Tmin) / (Tmax - Tmin))^5. The timer resets when the cookie dies. Tmin = ceil(30*60*5*m) and Tmax = ceil(30*60*15*m) frames, where m is the product of the frequency modifiers. Mean is about Tmin + 0.7094*T^(5/6) and median about Tmin + 0.7194*T^(5/6), where T = Tmax - Tmin in seconds.
curves.parameters: Base window 300-900 s. Lucky day x0.5 and Serendipity x0.5; Golden goose egg and Heavenly luck x0.95 each. My exact run of the per-frame process gives a base mean of 7.44 min, with 10th/median/90th percentiles of 6.81/7.48/8.03 min. With both x0.5 upgrades: mean 2.02 min (1.82-2.20). On-screen life is 13 s, x2 per Lucky day and Serendipity, and x0.95 for each other cookie on screen.
curves.purpose: A random timer that is not memoryless: nothing happens for 5 minutes, then a spawn becomes almost certain about 2.5 minutes later. Players can learn the rhythm and check in at the right time.
curves.source: https://orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js lines 5493-5510, 5458-5468, 5932-5991 (getTimeMod/getMinTime/getMaxTime), 5614-5622 (duration). Mean and median approximations: https://cookieclicker.fandom.com/wiki/Golden_Cookie (Spawn Time section)

curves.name: Golden and wrath cookie effects
curves.formula: Frenzy: CpS x7 for 77 s. Lucky: +min(0.15*bank, 900*CpS) + 13. Click frenzy: click power x777 for 13 s. Building special: CpS x(1 + owned/10) for 30 s, for a random building with 10 or more owned. Cookie storm: 7 s of drops, each worth max(1-7 minutes of CpS, 1-7 cookies). Chain: payouts of 7, 77, 777, ... capped at min(6 h of CpS, 0.5*bank); the chain breaks with 1% chance per step or at the cap. Wrath-only effects: Clot CpS x0.5 for 66 s; Ruin -min(0.05*bank, 600*CpS) - 13, never more than the bank; Elder frenzy x666 for 6 s; Cursed finger. Durations x2 with Get lucky.
curves.parameters: Effect pool for a golden cookie: [frenzy, multiply cookies], plus chain and storm with 3% chance (only after 100k cookies earned), click frenzy with about 10% chance, and building special with 25% chance once 10 or more buildings are owned. If the previous effect is in the pool, it is removed with 80% chance. The wrath pool is [clot, multiply cookies, ruin], plus a 30% chance to add blood frenzy, chain and storm. The wrath share is 1/3, 2/3 or all, by Grandmapocalypse stage (elderWrath 1/2/3).
curves.purpose: A random burst economy layered on top of steady production. Lucky rewards keeping a bank of at least 6,000 s of CpS. The anti-repeat rule keeps outcomes varied. Losses are capped by both bank share and production time.

curves.name: Wrinklers (deferred superlinear payout)
curves.formula: With n wrinklers attached, the player loses fraction n*0.05 of CpS. Every second, each wrinkler accumulates CpS * (n*0.05). Popping a wrinkler returns its total x1.1 (x3 more for a shiny one). With n = 10 the direct rate is 0.5*CpS, and the pops return about 10*0.5*1.1 = 5.5*CpS, so the total is about 6x.
curves.parameters: suckRate = 1/20 per wrinkler, toSuck = 1.1. Spawn chance per frame per empty slot is 0.00001*elderWrath.
curves.purpose: Patient, idle-friendly play gets a superlinear reward for leaving things alone and cashing in later.

curves.name: Prestige: heavenly chips and prestige level
curves.formula: prestige = floor( (cookiesBakedAllTime / 1e12)^(1/3) ). Inverse: cookies = chips^3 * 1e12. CpS multiplier term = +prestige * 0.01 * heavenlyPower * heavenlyMult, where heavenlyPower = 1. heavenlyMult starts at 0 and rises to 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 as Heavenly chip secret, Heavenly cookie stand, Heavenly bakery, Heavenly confectionery and Heavenly key are bought.
curves.parameters: HCfactor = 3. The first level needs 1e12 cookies baked all time; doubling prestige needs 8x the cookies. Potential-unlock prices: 11, 1,111, 111,111, 11,111,111 and 1,111,111,111 chips. Legacy (the first heavenly upgrade, which turns the system on) costs 1 chip. Twin Gates costs 1 and Perfect idling costs 7. Angel and demon upgrades cost 7^k. Spending chips does not lower the prestige level.
curves.purpose: A cube-root reset currency. Spending and the passive bonus are separate, so buying heavenly upgrades never weakens the next run.

curves.name: Offline production
curves.formula: Without Perfect idling or Twin Gates (and on the web, not mobile), nothing is earned while the game is closed. With Twin Gates: amount = (min(t, maxTime) + max(0, t - maxTime)*0.1) * CpS * percent/100. With Perfect idling: percent = 100 and the cap is effectively infinite.
curves.parameters: Base maxTime is 3,600 s, doubled by each of Belphegor, Mammon, Abaddon, Satan, Asmodeus, Beelzebub and Lucifer (up to 128 h). Base percent is 5, +10 for each of Angels, Archangels, Virtues, Dominions, Cherubim, Seraphim and God (up to 75). Chimera adds 2 days and +5%. Fern tea +3, Ichor syrup +7, Fortune #102 +1.
curves.purpose: Being away pays very little by default. Prestige upgrades buy back offline time and rate, so the game starts active and becomes more idle over time.

curves.name: Milk and kittens
curves.formula: milkProgress = achievementsOwned / 25. Each kitten upgrade multiplies CpS by (1 + milkProgress * k * milkMult), for example k = 0.1 for Kitten helpers and 0.125 for Kitten workers.
curves.parameters: milkMult starts at 1, x1.05 with Santa's milk and cookies, plus aura and god bonuses.
curves.purpose: A meta multiplier that turns breadth of play (achievements) into production.

curves.name: Business price (per-business coefficient)
curves.formula: cost of the next unit = initialCost * coefficient^owned. Bulk buys are just the sum, with no discount: sum over i of initialCost * coefficient^i. Pecorella's closed form: cost of n = b * r^k * (r^n - 1)/(r - 1). Max affordable = floor( log_r( c*(r-1)/(b*r^k) + 1 ) ).
curves.purpose: The coefficient falls with tier, from 1.15 at tier 2 to 1.07 at tier 10. Expensive late businesses therefore keep scaling for many more units: the 100th unit costs about 1.0e6 times the first for Newspaper but only 811 times for Oil.

curves.name: Milestone speed doublings
curves.formula: A business's cycle time halves at 25, 50, 100, 200, 300 and 400 owned. Capitalist unlocks halve all cycle times again when every business reaches 25, 50, 100, 200, 300 and 400. At most 12 halvings, so cycle time can fall to 1/4096 of the base. Beyond 400, unlocks multiply profit instead: Lemonade 500-900 gives x4 each, 1000 gives x5, and later ones give x2, x3 or x5. All-business unlocks from 500 up give profit x2.
curves.parameters: Newspaper unlocks also boost other businesses: 125 gives Lemonade x2, 150 Car Wash x2, 175 Pizza x2, 225 Donut x2, 250 Lemonade x3, 500 Shrimp x11, 600 Hockey x11, 700 Movie x11, 800 Bank x11, 900 Oil x11, 1000 Newspaper x7,777,777. Compare a milestone gap with the cost growth across it: 25 to 50 Lemonade multiplies the unit cost by 1.07^25 = 5.4, while output gains x2 from count and x2 from speed.
curves.purpose: Owned-count goals give spikes of satisfaction and steer which business to buy. The cross-boosting Newspaper keeps an early tier relevant.

curves.name: Cash upgrades
curves.formula: Upgrades bought with cash multiply profits, x3 for most and x7 for some later ones. They reset on prestige.
curves.parameters: Earth's first round, price then effect: Lemonade $250,000 x3; Newspaper $500,000 x3; Car Wash $1M x3; Pizza $5M x3; Donut $10M x3; Shrimp $25M x3; Hockey $500M x3; Movie $10B x3; Bank $50B x3; Oil $250B x3; Monopoly (all businesses) $1T x3. Later rounds repeat this, plus 'Angel Investor Effectiveness' +1% or +2% upgrades. The game has 464 cash upgrades in total.
curves.purpose: Fixed-price multiplier upgrades shorten the long gaps between milestones.

curves.name: Angel investors (prestige)
curves.formula: angelsGained = floor( sqrt(lifetimeEarnings / (4e11/9)) - sqrt(earningsInPreviousSessions / (4e11/9)) ), which is the same as 150*sqrt(lifetime/1e15) minus angels already earned. Bonus = +2% profit per unsacrificed angel, additive: 50 angels give x2 and 1,000 give x21.
curves.parameters: Divisor 4e11/9 = 4.444e10 on Earth and the Moon, and 1e11 on Mars. Thresholds for angels 1, 2 and 3: 44.44B, 177.78B and 400B lifetime. 1e15 lifetime gives 150 angels and 1e18 gives 4,743. Doubling the angel count needs 4x lifetime earnings. Angels spent on angel upgrades lose their 2% bonus.
curves.purpose: A square-root reset currency based on lifetime earnings, so a player can keep resetting at the same point and still gain a shrinking amount.

curves.name: Managers and offline progress
curves.formula: A manager restarts a business's cycle automatically, including while the player is disconnected. Managed businesses therefore earn at 100% offline.
curves.parameters: Earth manager prices: Lemonade 1,000 (about 267x the stand's base cost), Newspaper 15,000 (250x), Car Wash 100,000 (139x), Pizza 500,000 (58x), Donut 1.2M (11.6x), Shrimp 10M (8x), Hockey 111,111,111 (7.4x), Movie 555,555,555 (3.1x), Bank 10B (4.7x), Oil 100B (3.9x).
curves.purpose: Automation is a purchase. Before managers every cycle needs a click (active); after them the game is fully idle and offline earnings are full.

curves.name: Ad profit boost
curves.formula: Watching an ad doubles all profits for a few hours, and boosts stack up to a cap.
curves.parameters: x2 for 4 h per ad, up to about 24 h (from memory).
curves.purpose: A periodic check-in reward that pays active players without punishing idle ones.
curves.source: unconfirmed (from memory, not verified this session)

curves.name: Prestige (gems)
curves.formula: p = ( sqrt(1 + 8 * c_M / 1e12) - 1 ) / 2, where c_M is maximum earnings
curves.parameters: Doubling p needs about 4x the earnings. Resetting at the same point gives no new currency.
curves.purpose: A reset currency that grows like a triangular number.

curves.name: Prestige (soul eggs)
curves.formula: delta_p = ( c_R / 1e6 )^0.14, where c_R is earnings since the last reset
curves.parameters: Doubling needs about 128x the earnings.
curves.purpose: A reset currency with a very flat curve, so runs must go much deeper each time.

events: Cookie Clicker golden cookie, timing: base window 300-900 s. Each frame the spawn chance is ((t-Tmin)/(Tmax-Tmin))^5, so the mean wait is about Tmin + 0.71*T^(5/6), roughly 7.4 min (6.8-8.0 min for the 10th-90th percentile). The cookie stays on screen 13 s. The timer resets only after the cookie dies, so a missed cookie costs nothing beyond the lost chance. Source: main.js 5493-5510, 5932-5991.

Cookie Clicker golden cookie, positive outcomes: Frenzy (CpS x7 for 77 s, about 7.7 min of extra output), Lucky (+min(15% of bank, 15 min of CpS) + 13, best with a bank of 6,000 s of CpS), Click frenzy (clicks x777 for 13 s), Building special (CpS x(1 + n/10) for 30 s), Cookie chain, Cookie storm (7 s), and a free sugar lump at 0.05%. If the same effect as last time is in the pool, it is removed with 80% chance. Source: main.js 5680-5850.

Cookie Clicker wrath cookie, negative and mixed outcomes: Clot (CpS x0.5 for 66 s), Ruin (lose min(5% of bank, 10 min of CpS) + 13, never more than the bank), Cursed finger, and also Lucky, Elder frenzy (x666 for 6 s, 30% chance to enter the pool), chain and storm. The wrath share follows a player choice, the Grandmapocalypse stage: 1/3, 2/3 or all. Clicking a wrath cookie is optional, so ignoring it is always safe. Source: main.js 5549-5553, 5680-5810.

Cookie Clicker wrinklers: each one eats 5% of CpS while attached and pays back what it ate x1.1 when popped. Because each wrinkler eats the total share, 10 wrinklers return about 6x CpS. This is an idle event with a superlinear payout. Source: main.js 5338-5350, 14718, 14788-14798.

AdVenture Capitalist has no random events in the base loop. Its spikes are deterministic owned-count milestones (25/50/100/200/300/400 halve cycle time, and later counts multiply profit) plus timed ad boosts (unconfirmed: x2 for 4 h). Source: https://adventure-capitalist.fandom.com/wiki/Unlocks_(Earth)
pacing: First purchase: a Cookie Clicker Cursor costs 15 clicks, a Grandma 100, and the first click doubler 100. In AdCap you start owning one Lemonade Stand ($1 per 0.6 s) and the second costs $4, so the first purchase takes about 2.4 s. Both games make the first purchase almost instant.
Payback per tier roughly doubles. Cookie Clicker base payback runs 150 s (Cursor), 100, 138, 255, 500, 1000, 2564, 7500 s. AdCap runs 2.2, 3, 8, 24, 48, 192, 768, 3072, 12288 and 32056 s.
Tier ratios: Cookie Clicker price x10.8-16 and CpS x5.4-8 per tier. AdCap price x12 per tier, productivity x3-6, and cycle time x2-6 (0.6, 3, 6, 12, 24, 96, 384, 1536, 6144 and 36864 s).
Cost doubling per unit: ratio 1.15 doubles every 4.96 units, 1.10 every 7.27, and 1.07 every 10.24. Across a 25-unit milestone gap the cost grows x32.9 at 1.15, x10.8 at 1.10 and x5.4 at 1.07.

Milestones: Cookie Clicker doubles a building's output at 1/5/25/50/100 owned and then every 50. AdCap halves cycle time at 25/50/100/200/300/400, then multiplies profit every 100 (x2 to x5), with all-business versions of the same goals.

Golden cookie rhythm: about 7.4 min with no upgrades. With Lucky day and Serendipity the mean falls to about 2.0 min (Tmin 75 s, Tmax 225 s). A frequency upgrade is a strong lever for the active-play premium.

First prestige: one Cookie Clicker level at 1e12 cookies baked all time; the first AdCap angel at 4.44e10 lifetime and 150 angels (+300% profit) at 1e15. AdCap's first reset is generous, at about x4. Doubling the prestige currency takes 8x the earnings under a cube root, 4x under a square root, and 128x under Egg, Inc.'s exponent of 0.14.

Offline: Cookie Clicker on the web pays 0% by default, then 5% for 1 h through prestige upgrades (beyond that x0.1), and can reach 100% unlimited with Perfect idling (7 chips). AdCap pays 100% for managed businesses from the start.
prestige: Cookie Clicker: prestige = floor(cbrt(cookies baked all time / 1e12)). Each level adds +1% CpS times a potential factor, which upgrades raise to 5/25/50/75/100% for 11, 1,111, 111,111, 1.1e7 and 1.1e9 chips. Chips (gained equal to new prestige levels) are spent on a heavenly upgrade tree, and spending them does not lower the level, so the passive bonus is never lost. The first node, Legacy, costs 1 chip, so the first ascension always buys something. Source: main.js 4185-4231, 5175, 10516-10520, 11120.

AdVenture Capitalist: angels = floor(150*sqrt(lifetime/1e15)) minus angels already earned. The first angel comes at $44.44B and each angel adds +2% profit, additively. Angels can be sacrificed for angel upgrades, but a sacrificed angel stops giving its 2%. This is a real tradeoff, and a run can end up weaker if the player overspends. Lifetime-based, so the player can reset at the same point and still gain a little. Source: https://adventure-capitalist.fandom.com/wiki/Angel_Investors

Other prestige curves from Pecorella Part III: Realm Grinder p = (sqrt(1 + 8c/1e12) - 1)/2 on maximum earnings, and Egg, Inc. delta_p = (c_since_reset/1e6)^0.14. A square root needs 4x the earnings to double the reward, a cube root 8x, and an exponent of 0.14 about 128x. Source: https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/the-math-of-idle-games-part-iii

Pecorella's advice: vary the prestige cycle so runs have slow and fast stretches. Player reset timing is hard to predict, so model it across a range of parameters rather than as one optimal point. Source: Part III, URL above.
surveys.activeVsIdle: Cookie Clicker pays active players through four mechanics: golden cookies, banking for Lucky, Click frenzy combos, and clicks worth a share of CpS. From the code formulas, a player who catches every golden cookie at the base 7.4 min rhythm gains roughly 0.5*7.7 min (Frenzy) plus 0.5*(up to 15 min, Lucky) of output per 7.4 min. That is about +50% to +150% CpS depending on bank size. With Lucky day, Serendipity and Get lucky the premium becomes several times idle output, and Frenzy plus Click frenzy stacks pay far more. This estimate is my own calculation from the formulas, not a sourced figure. Idle play is supported by wrinklers (a superlinear patience payout, about 6x at 10 wrinklers) and by offline upgrades bought with prestige (5% for 1 h, rising to 100%). Missing a golden cookie only loses the chance; no penalty applies. AdVenture Capitalist pays active play only before managers, when every cycle needs a click, and through buy timing. After managers, idle and active earn almost the same and offline is 100%. Its only lasting active hook is the ad boost (unconfirmed). Lesson: Cookie Clicker keeps an active premium for the whole game by making active rewards optional chances on top of idle production. AdCap's premium disappears once automation is bought. toKin wants a lasting premium, so it should follow Cookie Clicker. My recommended target is that active play earns about 1.5x to 3x idle play, a smaller gap than Cookie Clicker's late game, so idle players still progress.
lessonsForToKin: TYPING LADDER (D3, D19): Use the Cookie Clicker geometric price. Level k costs B*r^(k-1) tokens while presses earn 2^(k-1) tokens, so level k takes B*(r/2)^(k-1) presses. Placeholder: B = 15, the same as Cookie Clicker's first Cursor, so the first buy is about 15 presses. With r = 3: cumulative presses to L8 (256 tokens per press) = 739, about 2 min at 6 presses/s or 4 min at 3/s. With r = 3.5: 1,739 presses (about 5-10 min). With r = 4: 3,825 presses (about 11-21 min). Recommend r = 3 to start, with a dev-panel slider from 2.5 to 4. Set the first computer's cap at L8 (a slider for L6-L10) as the D19 trigger for the first net.

PRESSES AFTER THE CAP (never soft-lock): Copy Cookie Clicker's mouse upgrades, where each click gains +1% of CpS per upgrade, and Thousand fingers, which adds +0.1 per building. Once the ladder caps, add research or hardware nodes that give each press +x% of current net tokens per second. Example: at 6 presses/s and 1% per press, pressing adds +6% of idle output per upgrade. Pressing then stays the permanent floor, never drops to zero, and keeps an active premium. Debuffs from events should never touch press income.

COPY COSTS (D5): Copy n of a net costs c0*r^n. Use r = 1.15 for the first net (Cookie Clicker; cost doubles every 4.96 copies). Then lower r for each newer net in the AdCap style: 1.15 for tier 2 down to 1.07 for tier 10, so later nets keep scaling. Suggested placeholders: Perceptron 1.15, multi-layer net 1.13, convolution 1.11, recurrence 1.09, attention 1.08, Transformer 1.07. Use Pecorella's closed forms for buy x10 and buy max: cost(n) = b*r^k*(r^n - 1)/(r - 1) and max = floor(log_r(c*(r-1)/(b*r^k) + 1)).

COPY MILESTONES AND DEDUP (D5): Cookie Clicker doubles at 1/5/25/50/100 owned and AdCap at 25/50/100/200/300/400. Put the 'copies start to repeat' event on the same milestones (for example 10/25/50/100 copies). When a net crosses one, copies above it lose output to repetition; one option is the birthday-style unique fraction S*(1 - (1 - 1/S)^n)/n with seed space S. Paying the dedup token cost restores output and grants the milestone's x2, turning AdCap's free doubling into an active choice. To prevent soft-lock, an unpaid dedup only lowers the marginal output of extra copies and never drops total output below its level before the milestone. Across a gap of 25 copies at r = 1.15 the cost rises x32.9 and milestones alone cannot keep pace, so research multipliers (backprop, dropout) must fill the rest, as AdCap's x3 cash upgrades do.

GIG MONEY (D6): Model gigs on AdCap businesses. Each gig has a cycle or deadline and a payout. Gig tiers rise about x12 in requirement and x3-6 in money per second, so payback grows x2-4 per tier (AdCap: 2.2, 3, 8, 24, 48, 192, 768 s). Deadlines can follow AdCap's cycle ladder, scaled to a 1900s town: about 30 s, 2 min, 5 min, 15 min, 1 h. Hand-starting gigs is the active path; a later 'client management' purchase acts like an AdCap manager (priced from about 270x down to about 4x the gig's base value) and automates them. Copy AdCap's Newspaper cross-boost: the newspaper gig's milestones could multiply other gigs' pay. A missed deadline should only forfeit that gig's payout, never money already held (Cookie Clicker's Ruin can never take more than the bank). Pause deadlines while offline.

HARDWARE AND COMPUTE (D7, D11, D15): Price repeat purchases of the same hardware at x1.15 per unit, like Cookie Clicker buildings. Hardware tiers should cost about x10-12 more and give about x5-8 more MIPS (Cookie Clicker early tiers: price x10.8-11, CpS x5.4-8; AdCap: price x12, productivity x3-6), so base payback roughly doubles per tier (Cookie Clicker: 100, 138, 255, 500, 1000 s). Allow selling hardware at 25% of its price (Cookie Clicker's refund) as a recovery path, which supports the never-soft-lock rule. Overclock crash events (D15) should use the capped-loss form: lose min(x% of the resource, y minutes of production), never more than held.

PIPELINES (D8, D16): Pecorella advises keeping older generators relevant and varying multipliers so that different generators lead at different stages. Give each converter its own multiplier track and occasional 'specials' like Cookie Clicker's Building special (x(1 + n/10) for 30 s for one building type). The best converter to invest in then changes over time, which gives active managers something to optimise. Keep the D16 (capacity/demand)^2 slowdown as the idle penalty. The D17 scheduler node then plays the role of AdCap's managers, bought automation that removes the active-only advantage for low-priority jobs.

PUBLISHING EVENTS (D10, D20): Reuse Cookie Clicker's shimmer timer. After a paper, roll each cost event with a per-tick chance of ((t - Tmin)/(Tmax - Tmin))^5; the mean is about Tmin + 0.71*T^(5/6). Suggested placeholder window: 120-360 s, a mean of about 3.1 min, so the costs land while the player is still around. Keep the 80% anti-repeat reroll so 'market catches up' and 'rival adopts your method' alternate. Cap each hit like Ruin: pay drop = min(p% of current pay, the value of m minutes of gigs), with p = 5 and m = 10 as placeholders, and never below a floor. Give each paper a fixed number of cost events (for example 2-3) so total cost is bounded and known. Like the Grandmapocalypse wrath ratio (1/3, 2/3, all), let the share of negative events grow with the number of recent papers, which gives the player a risk dial. Add golden-style positive events too, for example 'a famous lab cites you: gig pay x3 for 60 s' or 'Citations x7 for 77 s', so events give a reason to watch the tab.

SYNTHETIC DATA EVENT (brainstorm): The 'bad synthetic data, bad model' event fits Cookie Clicker's Clot (output x0.5 for 66 s) better than a permanent loss. Use a timed malus on that net's copies, with a data-cleaning branch that shortens or prevents it. That keeps the event recoverable.

DISTILL (D23): Use a square-root reset currency on lifetime tokens, as AdCap and Realm Grinder do (doubling the reward needs 4x the progress). A cube root (Cookie Clicker, 8x) would feel stingier. Placeholder: DistillPoints = floor(k*sqrt(L/L0)) minus points already earned, with L0 = lifetime tokens when Distill unlocks (a short while after the first AI paper) and k = 10 on a dev slider. The first Distill then gives about 10 points, and waiting until 4x L0 gives 20. Each point gives a permanent multiplier; AdCap uses +2% additive and Cookie Clicker +1% per level. Make the first reset feel strong (AdCap's first reset is about x4); aim for at least x1.5-2 speed on run 2. Follow Cookie Clicker's split, not AdCap's: the Distill level gives the passive bonus permanently, and spending points on the Distill tree never lowers it. AdCap's 'sacrificed angels stop giving 2%' can make the next run weaker, a soft-lock risk. Make the first tree node cost 1 point, like Legacy, so the first Distill always buys something. Keep the reward lifetime-based, so resetting at the same point still pays a little (AdCap) and a stuck player can always Distill forward.

OFFLINE AND BACKGROUND TABS: Cookie Clicker pays 0% offline by default and upgrades to 5% for 1 h, then up to 100% with Perfect idling. AdCap pays 100% for managed businesses. Recommended toKin placeholder: simulate offline time with the player's current job queue and the D16 slowdown, so setting priorities before leaving pays off. Start at a reduced rate (for example 50%) with a cap (for example 8 h), and add research nodes that raise both, the way Cookie Clicker's angels and demons do. Beyond the cap apply x0.1, as Cookie Clicker does. Compute progress from wall-clock timestamps, not per-frame ticks, because browsers throttle background tabs (an engineering note, not from a source). Never let a deadline or event fire against an absent player.

ACTIVE VS IDLE: Cookie Clicker keeps an active premium all game, about +50% to +150% CpS at base golden cookie frequency by my calculation from the code, and several times more with frequency upgrades. AdCap's premium disappears once managers are bought. Target active at about 1.5x to 3x idle, tunable. Make active rewards optional chances (golden-style events, pipeline tuning, press bonuses) rather than penalties for absence, apart from the agreed D16 slowdown, which the D17 scheduler lets idle players buy out of. Give idle players a patience payout like Cookie Clicker's wrinklers, about 6x at 10. Citations already fit: they accrue over time and could be collected in a lump.

DEV PANEL: Expose these as sliders with the recommended defaults: ladder B (15) and r (3), ladder cap level (8), copy ratio per net (1.15 down to 1.07), milestone counts (10/25/50/100) and multiplier (x2), hardware unit ratio (1.15), tier price ratio (x11) and MIPS ratio (x6), the golden-style event window (Tmin 120 s, Tmax 360 s, exponent 5, anti-repeat 0.8), event loss caps (5% of pay, 10 min), Distill k (10), exponent (0.5) and bonus per point (2%), and offline rate (50%), cap (8 h) and beyond-cap factor (0.1).

games: Antimatter Dimensions (IvarK et al., Reality-era source on GitHub: github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode, master branch, read directly)
Clicker Heroes (Playsaurus; formulas from clickerheroes.fandom.com, read through the MediaWiki api.php wikitext endpoint because the HTML pages sit behind a Cloudflare check)
Realm Grinder (Divine Games; formulas from realm-grinder.fandom.com, read the same way)
Cross-game reference: Anthony Pecorella, 'The Math of Idle Games' parts I and III (Kongregate, republished on gamedeveloper.com)

curves.name: Antimatter Dimension base costs and per-set cost multipliers
curves.formula: Price of the next set of 10 = BaseCost[t] * BaseInc[t]^(floor(bought/10)). Every unit within a set of 10 costs the same. BaseCost = [10, 100, 1e4, 1e6, 1e9, 1e13, 1e18, 1e24] and BaseInc = [1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e8, 1e10, 1e12, 1e15] for tiers 1 to 8. Past Number.MAX_VALUE (1.79e308) a super-exponential term is added: log10 cost += 0.5*excess*(excess+1)*log10(costScale), with costScale = 10 by default.
curves.purpose: Cost of tiered generators. Higher tiers start much higher and scale much faster.
curves.parameters: The player starts with 10 antimatter. dimensionMultDecrease = 10 - upgrades (cache.js). The scaling threshold is 1.79e308.
curves.source: https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode/blob/master/src/core/dimensions/antimatter-dimension.js (lines ~337-363); ExponentialCostScaling in https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode/blob/master/src/core/math.js; start antimatter DC.E1 in src/core/player.js

curves.name: Buy-10 multiplier
curves.formula: Dimension multiplier *= buyTenMultiplier^(floor(bought/10)), with buyTenMultiplier = 2 at base (raised by Infinity upgrades and achievements)
curves.purpose: A milestone multiplier. Each completed set of 10 doubles the tier's output, so cost x1e3 per set is answered by output x2 per set plus the cascade.
curves.parameters: base 2

curves.name: Generator cascade (each tier produces the tier below)
curves.formula: productionPerSecond[t] = amount[t] * multiplier[t] * Tickspeed.perSecond. Tier 1 adds that much antimatter per second. Tier t+1 adds productionPerSecond[t+1]/10 units of tier t per second (tick calls produceDimensions(..., diff/10)).
curves.purpose: Tier stacking gives polynomial growth of rising degree (about t^n for n tiers) before any multipliers.
curves.parameters: 1/10 transfer factor between tiers. Tickspeed.perSecond = 1000 / current tick in ms (the tick starts at 1000 ms).

curves.name: Tickspeed (global speed upgrade)
curves.formula: Cost = 1000 * 10^k for the k-th purchase (costScale 10 after 1.79e308). Tick interval = 1000ms * mult^purchases. With 0 galaxies mult = 1/1.1245, so each purchase gives x1.1245 speed. With 1 galaxy mult = 1/1.11888888, with 2 galaxies 1/1.11267177. With 3 or more galaxies mult = 0.8 * 0.965^(galaxies-2-2) after the galaxy count is scaled by effects. Below 3 galaxies, each galaxy also subtracts 0.02.
curves.purpose: One multiplier that speeds every generator: a price of x10 per step buys x1.12 speed. Six buys (up to 1e8) roughly double speed (x2.02).
curves.parameters: base cost 1000, cost ratio 10, speed factor 1.1245

curves.name: Dimension Boost (soft reset 1)
curves.formula: Requirement: 20 dimensions of tier min(boosts+3, 8). Once tier 8 is reached the requirement is 20 + (boosts-5)*15 eighth dimensions. Effect: each tier t gets 2^(boosts+1-t), clamped to at least 1. A boost resets antimatter, dimensions and tickspeed.
curves.purpose: A gated reset that unlocks the next tier and adds a permanent x2 per boost.
curves.parameters: DimBoost.power = 2 at base, increment 15 per boost after tier 8

curves.name: Antimatter Galaxy (soft reset 2)
curves.formula: Requirement = 80 + 60*galaxies eighth dimensions. From 100 galaxies ('distant') add g^2+g. From 800 ('remote') multiply by 1.002^(g-799). A galaxy resets Dimension Boosts and makes each tickspeed purchase stronger.
curves.purpose: A second gate that strengthens the global speed multiplier. It is the pattern for a big hardware jump that improves every later small upgrade.
curves.parameters: baseCost 80, costMult 60, distant start 100, remote start 800

curves.name: Dimensional Sacrifice
curves.formula: 8th dimension multiplier = max(1, log10(totalSacrificedAntimatter)/10)^2 before Infinity Challenge 2. Sacrifice is unlocked after 5 Dimension Boosts.
curves.purpose: An optional mini reset that trades lower tiers for a permanent multiplier on the top tier. It is an active-play lever.
curves.parameters: exponent 2 at base, divisor 10

curves.name: Infinity Points (prestige 1)
curves.formula: Before Break Infinity, production stops at 2^1024 = 1.79e308 and the only action left is a Big Crunch, which gives 308/308 = 1 IP times IP multipliers. After Break Infinity, IP = floor(10^(log10(maxAntimatter)/308 - 0.75) * mult). That gives 1.78 IP at 1e308 and 17.8 IP at 1e616.
curves.purpose: A first prestige forced by a hard cap that always pays a fixed minimum. Later the gain becomes log-scaled with no cap.
curves.parameters: divisor 308 (reduced by Achievement 103 and Time Study 111), offset 0.75
curves.source: https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode/blob/master/src/game.js (gainedInfinityPoints); production halt in antimatter-dimension.js tick ('Stop producing antimatter at Big Crunch goal')

curves.name: Eternity Points and Reality Machines (prestige 2 and 3)
curves.formula: EP = floor(5^(log10(IP)/308 - 0.7) * mult). RM = floor(1000^(log10(EP)/4000 - 1) * mult), replaced by the linear 27/4000*log10(EP) - 26 when the result falls between 1 and 10. Reality needs EP of at least 1e4000.
curves.purpose: Each layer takes the log of the layer below with a new base, which compresses about 300 orders of magnitude into one digit of the next currency.
curves.parameters: EP base 5, offset 0.7. RM base 1000, divisor 4000.

curves.name: Active / Passive / Idle time studies (mutually exclusive)
curves.formula: Let f(t) = 15^(ln(10t+1) * min((10t+1)^0.125, 500)), with t = seconds in the current Infinity. TS141 (active) gives x1e45/f(t), which decays. TS142 (passive) gives a flat x1e25. TS143 (idle) gives x f(t), which grows. For EP: TS121 (active) gives clamp(250/avgSecondsPerEternity, 1, 50), TS122 (passive) gives x35, TS123 (idle) gives sqrt(1.39 * secondsThisEternity).
curves.purpose: An explicit three-way playstyle choice. Computed crossovers: active beats passive while runs stay under about 115 s, idle beats passive after about 272 s, and active equals idle at about 180 s (both about 1e22.5). For EP, idle beats passive x35 after 881 s and beats the active x50 after 1799 s.
curves.parameters: f(t) caps at exponent factor 500. The flat values are 1e25 and 35.
curves.source: https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode/blob/master/src/core/secret-formula/eternity/time-studies/normal-time-studies.js (thisInfinityMult, passiveIPMult, ids 121-123 and 141-143). Crossover times computed in scratch.

curves.name: Time-played multipliers (idle-friendly Infinity upgrades)
curves.formula: timeMult: (totalMinutesPlayed/2)^0.15. timeMult2: max((minutesThisInfinity/4)^0.25, 1). An unspent-IP multiplier on Dimension 1: (IP/2)^1.5 + 1.
curves.purpose: Gentle power-law rewards for time and for banking currency.
curves.parameters: exponents 0.15, 0.25, 1.5

curves.name: Autobuyer upgrade curve
curves.formula: Base interval is [500, 600, ..., 1200] ms for dimensions 1 to 8. Each upgrade sets interval *= 0.6 (floor 100 ms) and cost *= 2, paid in IP and starting at 1 IP.
curves.purpose: Automation is earned through the prestige currency. Idle play buys its way to active-level throughput.
curves.parameters: interval x0.6 per level, cost x2 per level, floor 100 ms

curves.name: Hero level cost
curves.formula: cost(level -> level+1) = floor(floor(BaseCost * 1.07^level) * CostReduction). For Cid: floor((5+level) * 1.07^(level-1)) for levels 1-15, then floor(20 * 1.07^(level-1)). The four Ace Scouts use 1.22 instead of 1.07.
curves.purpose: Exponential cost of a generator that only grows linearly. Cost roughly doubles every 10 levels (1.07^10 = 1.97).
curves.parameters: growth 1.07 (1.22 for Ace Scouts). Dogcog reduces the cost (level 7 gives -6.69%).

curves.name: Hero DPS and level milestones
curves.formula: DPS = BaseDPS * level * 4^(floor((level-200)/25)+1 for level >= 200), with x10 at levels 1000, 2000, ..., 8000. Heroes after Frostleaf get x5 per 25 levels from 525 to 725. Xavira-era heroes get x4.5 per 25 levels and no x10. Ace Scouts get x1000 per 25 levels. Effective gain per level after 200 is 4^(1/25) = 1.057 against a cost growth of 1.07, so each level is about 1.2% less efficient.
curves.purpose: Milestone multipliers keep old generators relevant while costs slowly outrun the gains. That pushes the player toward the next hero.
curves.parameters: x4 per 25 levels, x10 per 1000 levels up to 8000, global DPS bonuses total x80.677

curves.name: Monster HP and gold by zone
curves.formula: HP for zones 1-140: ceil(10*(z-1+1.55^(z-1))), x10 for bosses. Zones 141-500: ceil(10*(139+1.55^139*1.145^(z-140))). Above 500 the growth rate is 1.145 + 0.001*floor((i-1)/500) per zone. Gold rises x1.60255 per zone up to zone 140, then 4.717e28 * 1.15^(z-140), x10 for bosses.
curves.purpose: The income-versus-difficulty race. Gold grows x1.15 per zone against HP at x1.145 and costs at x1.07 per level, so the player gains about 2.07 hero levels per zone (ln 1.15 / ln 1.07).
curves.parameters: HP growth 1.55 then 1.145. Gold growth 1.60255 then 1.15. Boss multiplier x10.
curves.source: https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Formulas (Monster HP for levels, Monster Gold Worth)

curves.name: Zone scaling (boss deadline)
curves.formula: Boss timer = 30 - 2*floor(z/500) s. Monsters per zone = 10 + 0.1*floor(z/500). Boss HP = (10 + 0.2*floor(z/500)) regular monsters. Treasure chest chance = 0.01*e^(-0.004*floor(z/500)). Primal boss chance = 0.25 - 0.02*floor(z/500).
curves.purpose: A timed gate that tightens slowly. Failing it just sends the player back to farm. It never locks.
curves.parameters: 30 s base timer, -2 s per 500 zones

curves.name: Click damage against DPS
curves.formula: Base click comes from Cid's upgrades (+100% to +250% each, Cid's click only). Some heroes add an upgrade worth +0.5% of total DPS per upgrade, up to 3.5% of DPS in total. Crit chance is 0% by default (3 upgrades of +3%), crit multiplier is x10 by default (x18 with upgrades). Fragsworth adds +20% click per level, Bhaal +15% crit damage per level. Hero souls give +10% DPS each and Cid's click benefits.
curves.purpose: Keeps clicking meaningful after Cid falls off by tying the click to a fraction of idle DPS.
curves.parameters: 0.5% of DPS per upgrade, 3.5% cap, crit x10 to x18

curves.name: Idle ancients (Siyalatas, Libertas) and the idle-state rule
curves.formula: Siyalatas: +25% DPS per level while idle, the per-level gain dropping 1% every 10 levels down to 15%. Libertas: the same curve for gold while idle. Idle starts after 60 s with no click and is cancelled by 2 clicks within 5 minutes (one misclick is tolerated). Both cost n hero souls for level n. Xyliqil (Outsider) multiplies idle bonuses by 1.5^level. Optimal Siyalatas level is sqrt(10*HS/(24+15*R^2)) with R about 0.926 early, which gives level 16.5 at 1e3 HS and 521 at 1e6 HS.
curves.purpose: Explicit idle bonuses switched on by inactivity, so idle and active become exclusive states.
curves.parameters: +25% to +15% per level, 60 s idle trigger, 2 clicks per 5 min cancel

curves.name: Juggernaut combo (active streak)
curves.formula: FinalDPS = DPS * (1 + stacks * 0.0001 * level). The combo starts at 3 stacks after 3 clicks and adds +1 per click. It holds for 280 s without clicking, then decays by 5% of the combo per second. Cost per level is n^1.5. Cumulative cost is about 0.4*n^2.5.
curves.purpose: A streak reward that grows without limit while the player clicks at least once every 4m40s, with a generous grace period.
curves.parameters: +0.01% per level per stack, 280 s grace, 5%/s decay

curves.name: Ancient level costs
curves.formula: Most ancients cost n hero souls for level n, so the cumulative cost is about n^2/2 (linear-cost family). Juggernaut and Solomon cost n^1.5 (cumulative about 0.4*n^2.5). Morgulis costs a flat 1 HS per level for +11% DPS. Respec refunds 75% of spent hero souls.
curves.purpose: Spending sinks for the prestige currency with different curvatures, plus one flat 'bank' sink.
curves.parameters: cost exponents 1, 1.5, 0; respec refund 75%

curves.name: Ascension: hero souls (prestige 1)
curves.formula: Hero souls on ascension = floor(totalHeroLevels/2000) + the sum over primal bosses killed of floor(((z-80)/25)^1.3 * (1+Ponyboy)). For transcended players, primal bosses also give 20*(1+Ponyboy)*(1+TP)^(z/5-20). Each unspent hero soul gives +10% DPS (formula term 1 + HS*0.1 + Morgulis*0.11). Ascension unlocks at Amenhotep level 150.
curves.purpose: A prestige currency from both breadth (hero levels) and depth (zone reached). The breadth term guarantees a floor.
curves.parameters: 2000 levels per soul, exponent 1.3, offset 80, divisor 25, +10% per unspent soul

curves.name: Transcendence: ancient souls and transcendent power (prestige 2)
curves.formula: AS = floor(5 * log10(total HS sacrificed)), so +5 AS per 10x hero souls. TP = 25 - 23*e^(-0.0003*AS) %, an asymptote of 25%. Chor'gorloth cuts ancient costs by (1 - 0.95^level), capped at level 150. Ponyboy adds +1000*level^2 % primal hero souls. Transcendence is available after zone 300.
curves.purpose: A log-compressed second layer whose currency upgrades the first layer's income.
curves.parameters: 5 per decade, TP max 25%, decay constant 0.0003

curves.name: Active skills (cooldown boosts)
curves.formula: Clickstorm: 10 clicks/s for 30 s, 10 min cooldown. Powersurge: +100% DPS for 30 s, 10 min. Lucky Strikes: +50% crit chance for 30 s, 30 min. Metal Detector: +100% gold for 30 s, 30 min. Golden Clicks: each click gives 1% of the monster's gold for 30 s, 1 h. Dark Ritual: x1.05 DPS permanently for the run, up to 20 stacks, 8 h. Super Clicks: +200% click for 30 s, 1 h. Energize: doubles the next skill, 1 h. Reload: -1 h on the last skill's cooldown, 1 h.
curves.purpose: Active-play windows that reward returning at cooldown boundaries.
curves.parameters: 30 s durations, 10 min to 8 h cooldowns

curves.name: Auto Clicker price
curves.formula: cost_n = 1000 + 500*n rubies, total 250*n*(3+n)
curves.purpose: A linear-cost automation of the active mechanic.
curves.parameters: 1000 base, +500 each

curves.name: Building cost and production
curves.formula: cost_x = BaseCost * 1.15^x before Ascension and BaseCost * 1.03^x after. Base costs and base production by tier 1-11: Farm 10 / 2, Inn 125 / 6, Blacksmith 600 / 20, tier 4 1,800 / 65, tier 5 5,600 / 200, tier 6 38,000 / 650, tier 7 442,000 / 2,000, tier 8 7.3M / 8,500, tier 9 145M / 100,000, tier 10 3.2B / 1.2M, Hall of Legends 200B / 250,000 per trophy.
curves.purpose: Flat-tier generators (no cascade) with a single growth ratio. A reset layer flattens the ratio.
curves.parameters: ratio 1.15, then 1.03 after Ascension

curves.name: Building milestone upgrades
curves.formula: Tier 1 (Farm) upgrades: at 5 owned, cost 200, +100%. At 25 owned, 6,580, +200%. At 75 owned, 10.7M, +300%. At 150 owned, 509B, +400%. Tier 4 and above get +100% per milestone. The first two milestones of each building (5th and 25th) each give 1 assistant.
curves.purpose: Count milestones that give multipliers and unlock a side resource (assistants).
curves.parameters: milestones 5 / 25 / 75 / 150 ...

curves.name: Clicks and assistants
curves.formula: One click gives 1 coin plus 'Clicking Reward' upgrades. Each assistant passively 'clicks' once per second for 5% of the clicking reward. Manual clicks are capped at 30 per second. Automatic clicks come from upgrades (Sun Blessing 15/s during Moon Blessing, Elven Bloodline 3/s at x100 reward, research C590 10/s, Sturdy Treasure +1/s offline each). Elf 'Sylvan Treasure Frills' adds 50% of total building production to the base click. Fairy 'Golden Pots' adds 100% of Farm, Inn and Blacksmith production.
curves.purpose: Clicks are tied to production so the active player keeps a meaningful edge. Assistants turn click power into idle income.
curves.parameters: 5% of click per assistant per second; 30 clicks/s manual cap

curves.name: Spells and mana (active layer)
curves.formula: Mana capacity 1000 and regeneration 1.0/s at base. Tax Collection: 200 mana, instantly gives 30 s of production. Call to Arms: 400 mana, 20 s, +0.3*buildings^0.975 %. Holy Light (Good): 900 mana, 10 s, +2500% click. Blood Frenzy (Evil): 600 mana, 20 s, +1000% Evil buildings. Gem Grinder (Neutral): 1000 mana, 20 s, +5000% gem bonus. Brainwave (Faceless): 600 mana, 600 s, +2% cumulative per second (+1200% by the end). Combo Strike (Drow): +30*casts^0.9 % per consecutive cast.
curves.purpose: Short, strong active buffs on a regenerating meter, plus long ramping buffs that suit idle play.
curves.parameters: mana 1000 cap, 1/s regen; durations 10-600 s

curves.name: Faction playstyle formulas (active vs idle)
curves.formula: Good factions are active and Evil factions are idle. Elf (active): Moon Blessing gives +1.75*ln(1+totalClicks)^3.1 %, and Secret Clicking Techniques gives +2*clicksThisR^0.4 %. Angel (active): God's Hand gives +150 x mana regen for 20 s. Undead (idle): heritage gives floor(1 + 1.5*sqrt(hoursThisGame)) assistants (1 h: 2, 4 h: 4, 24 h: 8), and Unholy Rituals gives +0.4*offlineSec^0.8 %. Demon (idle): bloodline gives +floor(0.04*evilSeconds^0.8)% to the gem bonus. Goblin (idle): cheap buildings, heritage +floor(7.5*log(1+gems))%, and Green Fingers Discount gives randRange(1,2500) x production every 30 s, even offline. Faceless (time): heritage gives +0.25*maxBuildings^0.75 %.
curves.purpose: Whole-build active or idle identities, chosen per run (affiliation). Idle factions scale on elapsed or offline time and active factions on click or spell counts.
curves.parameters: mostly power laws with exponents 0.4-0.8 on time, and ln^k on counts

curves.name: Druid Grand Balance (balance reward)
curves.formula: The least productive building gets +round(0.25*(x*y*z/729)^0.9) multiplier, where x, y and z are the counts of the three most-built buildings. Cost 1000 mana (800 upgraded), 20 s.
curves.purpose: Rewards keeping several production lines balanced. Maps directly onto pipeline bottleneck management.
curves.parameters: exponent 0.9, normaliser 729 (9^3)

curves.name: Royal Exchange (spend side currency on additive boosts)
curves.formula: Each exchange gives +10% to all building production, additive across exchanges. The next exchange costs floor(20 * 1.1^x) faction coins. Buying from x to y costs 200*(1.1^y - 1.1^x).
curves.purpose: An open-ended sink that turns surplus specialised currency into a slowly diminishing global boost.
curves.parameters: +10% each, cost base 20, ratio 1.1

curves.name: Faction coin find chance
curves.formula: Base 10% per click. Every 100% of chance gives one guaranteed coin and the remainder is the chance of one more (137% gives 1 coin plus 37% for a second).
curves.purpose: A probabilistic drop that stays smooth at high values.
curves.parameters: base 10%

curves.name: Gems (prestige 1, Abdication)
curves.formula: The n-th gem needs n*1e12 more coins, so the total for n gems is n*(n+1)*5e11 and n = (sqrt(1+8c/1e12) - 1)/2, about sqrt(c/5e11). That gives 1 gem at 1e12, 44 at 1e15 and 1,414 at 1e18. Doubling gems needs 4x the coins. Each gem gives +2% production through Gem Power, with +1% more each from Potency, Supremacy and Sovereignty. Abdication is allowed at any time, even when it gives nothing.
curves.purpose: A square-root prestige. Resetting at the same point earns nothing new (it is based on max coins), so each run has to go further.
curves.parameters: 5e11 coefficient, square root

curves.name: Reincarnation and Ascension (prestige 2 and 3)
curves.formula: The first Reincarnation needs 1e27 gems and each later one costs 1000x more. Gems reset in exchange for Reincarnation Power perks: +50%*R production, +500%*R offline production, +R% faction coin chance, mana regen floor(6.25*(sqrt(1+8R)-1))/10; from R10, +R^1.75 * t^0.65 % (t = total hours); from R20, +0.01%*R per building of the same type. Ascension happens at R39, R99, R159 and R219. It switches buildings to 1.03 growth and shrinks every income multiplier m to m^(1/10) (6000% becomes x1.508). Post-Ascension gem requirement: 1e27^(A^0.75) * 100^(R-40).
curves.purpose: Escalating reset thresholds with perks that grow linearly in the count. Ascension is also a number-range rescale.
curves.parameters: x1000 per Reincarnation; Ascension exponent 0.1

curves.name: Generic generator cost, bulk-buy and max-affordable
curves.formula: cost_next = base * r^owned. production = base_prod * owned * multipliers. Bulk cost of n units with k owned = b * r^k * (r^n - 1)/(r - 1). Max affordable = floor(log_r(c*(r-1)/(b*r^k) + 1)). AdVenture Capitalist Lemonade Stand: r = 1.07, base cost about 4 (3.738), 1.67/s, stacking x2 at 25 and 50 owned.
curves.purpose: Closed-form math for the dev panel and the balance bot.
curves.parameters: r is commonly 1.07 to 1.15 (that range is unconfirmed as a stated rule; 1.07 is confirmed for AdCap, 1.07 for CH, 1.15 for RG)

curves.name: Prestige gain formulas compared
curves.formula: Realm Grinder: p = (sqrt(1+8*cMax/1e12) - 1)/2, 4x earnings to double. Cookie Clicker: p = cbrt(cLifetime/1e12), 8x to double. AdVenture Capitalist: p = 150*sqrt(cLifetime/1e15), about 3-4x. Egg, Inc.: delta p = (cRun/1e6)^0.14, 128x per the article (computed 2^(1/0.14) is about 141x).
curves.purpose: Choosing the prestige exponent sets how many times more a player must earn to double the reward.
curves.parameters: exponent 1/2, 1/3 or 0.14

surveys.activeVsIdle:
All three games pay active play more per hour than idle play, and each builds idle play as a full second style. They do it in different ways.

Clicker Heroes uses state switches. Idle mode starts after 60 s without a click and ends after 2 clicks in 5 minutes. Idle ancients (Siyalatas +25% DPS and Libertas +25% gold per level, falling to 15%) work only in that state. Active ancients (Fragsworth +20% click per level, Bhaal +15% crit per level, Juggernaut +0.01% x level per combo stack, with a 280 s grace) need clicking. Click damage also takes up to 3.5% of DPS from hero upgrades. The wiki ranks Active above Hybrid above Idle and says Idle 'caps out' around zone 182k. Hybrid idles until monsters stop dying instantly, then plays actively.

Realm Grinder puts the split into faction identity. Good factions (Elf, Fairy, Angel) scale on clicks, spells and mana. Evil factions (Goblin, Undead, Demon) scale on elapsed, offline and Evil time, for example Undead gaining floor(1 + 1.5*sqrt(hours)) assistants. Neutral factions mix both, and Faceless Brainwave ramps +2%/s over 600 s. Assistants turn click power into idle income at 5% of click reward per second each. Manual clicks are capped at 30/s.

Antimatter Dimensions makes it a three-way exclusive purchase. TS141 (active) gives x1e45/f(t) and decays with run time, TS142 (passive) gives a flat x1e25, and TS143 (idle) gives f(t) and grows. Active wins for runs under about 115 s, idle wins after about 272 s, and the two meet near 180 s. EP studies 121 to 123 follow the same pattern (x50 for fast eternities, x35 flat, sqrt(1.39 t)). AD also lets idle play buy automation: autobuyer interval x0.6 per upgrade at 2x IP cost, down to 100 ms.

Shared patterns:
1. Active bonuses are big multipliers on short windows (30 s skills, 10-20 s spells) or on click counts.
2. Idle bonuses are power laws in time, with exponents 0.25 to 0.8 or sqrt.
3. The style choice is exclusive per run or per build, so neither style is strictly better.
4. Clicks keep some value late by taking a share of passive output.
5. Automation that closes the gap is bought with prestige currency, so idle play earns its way up. toKin's D17 scheduler node follows this same shape.
events: Realm Grinder keeps several separate pseudorandom generators. Lightning Strike, Dragon's Breath, Excavation, Green Fingers Discount and Miracle each have their own seeded stream, and those states are stored in the save file. Reloading or re-importing a save does not re-roll outcomes, and outcomes can be forecast. Source: https://realm-grinder.fandom.com/wiki/Random_Number_Generator

Realm Grinder Goblin 'Green Fingers Discount' gives coins every 30 s equal to randRange(1,2500) x total production per second. It also works offline. Source: https://realm-grinder.fandom.com/wiki/Goblin

Realm Grinder Elven Luck: each click has a 1% chance to give 10000% of production, and manual clicks give more. Star Blessing adds a 5% chance on Sun Blessing autoclicks for 250000% of production plus 1000 faction coins. Source: https://realm-grinder.fandom.com/wiki/Elf

Realm Grinder Titan Lightning Strike multiplies the production of one random building by 300% per Iron Stronghold. The wiki calls it 'very powerful... when lucky'. Source: https://realm-grinder.fandom.com/wiki/Spells and https://realm-grinder.fandom.com/wiki/Factions

Realm Grinder spell unlocks tied to real-world time: True Night means casting Night Time between 11 pm and 6 am, Sun Blessing means casting Moon Blessing between 6 am and 12 pm, God's Rest means casting God's Hand on a Sunday. Source: https://realm-grinder.fandom.com/wiki/Undead , /wiki/Elf , /wiki/Angel

Clicker Heroes primal bosses: on the first visit to a boss zone from zone 100, there is a 25% chance of a primal boss, minus 0.02 per 500 zones. Centennial bosses at zones 100-1000 are always primal. A primal boss pays floor(((z-80)/25)^1.3) hero souls. Source: https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Formulas and https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Hero_Souls

Clicker Heroes treasure chests: a 1% chance, times 0.994 every 500 zones, of a chest worth 10x gold, more with Mimzee. A random gild is granted at zone 100 and then every 10 zones, once per transcension. Source: https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Formulas and https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Heroes

Clicker Heroes deadline: bosses must be killed within 30 s, minus 2 s per 500 zones. A failed boss sends the player back to farm, so the deadline is never a lock. Source: https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Formulas

Antimatter Dimensions: I found no random production events in the core files I read. Its pacing events are deterministic thresholds: Dimension Boost, Galaxy, the Infinity cap at 1.79e308, and challenges. (unconfirmed for the whole codebase)
pacing: AD first tier: start with 10 antimatter. Dimension 1 costs 10, and a set of 10 costs 1,000 per unit after the first set. Each set of 10 doubles the tier's output. Cost per set rises x1e3 to x1e15 depending on tier. Tier n+1 feeds tier n at 1/10 of its own rate. Source: antimatter-dimension.js
AD global speed: tickspeed costs 1,000 then x10 per buy, and each buy gives x1.1245 speed. That reaches about x2 speed after 6 buys at 1e8. Galaxies make each tick buy stronger. Source: tickspeed.js

AD gates: a Dimension Boost needs 20 of the newest tier. After all 8 tiers it needs 20 + 15 per extra boost of tier 8. A Galaxy needs 80 + 60 per galaxy of tier 8. Before Break Infinity the run ends hard at 1.79e308 for exactly 1 IP. Source: dimboost.js, galaxy.js, game.js

CH: hero levels cost x1.07 each (x1.97 per 10 levels). DPS gets x4 per 25 levels from level 200, so the optimal pattern is to keep each hero about 25 levels above the next one. Gold rises x1.15 per zone after zone 140 against HP at x1.145, which works out to about 2.07 hero levels per zone. Source: Formulas wiki

CH skills put active play on a clock. The core 30 s buffs come back every 10 min (Clickstorm, Powersurge), 30 min (Lucky Strikes, Metal Detector) or 1 h (Golden Clicks, Super Clicks, Energize, Reload). Dark Ritual is on 8 h. Source: Skills wiki

RG: buildings cost x1.15 each, with milestone multipliers at 5, 25, 75 and 150 owned (+100%, +200%, +300% and +400% for Farms). Each of the first two milestones also gives an assistant. The first gem comes at 1e12 coins, and doubling gems takes 4x the coins. The first Reincarnation needs 1e27 gems and each later one costs x1000. Source: Buildings, Upgrades: Buildings, Gems, Reincarnation wikis
RG mana: 1000 cap and 1/s regen, so a 200-mana Tax Collection is ready every 200 s. That paces active spell windows at a few minutes apart. Source: Mana and Spells wikis

Pecorella's AdCap example: a generator with r = 1.07 and x2 multipliers at 25 and 50 owned. Exponential costs against linear production make each generator stall in turn, which hands progress to the next tier or to prestige. Source: gamedeveloper.com Math of Idle Games part I

Presses per level grow as (r/2)^L. Scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-toKin/25254004-8b9c-5eba-aff1-2f239458dc4c/scratchpad/curves/sim/ladder.py

Computed copy counts (base 100 tokens, cost ratio g): with 1e6 tokens you can afford 96 copies at g=1.07, 72 at 1.10 and 52 at 1.15. With 1e8 tokens: 164, 120 and 85. Source: Pecorella max-affordable formula
prestige: AD layer 0.5, Dimension Boost: a soft reset of antimatter, dimensions and tickspeed for a permanent 2^(boosts+1-t) on tier t. It also unlocks tiers 5 to 8. Source: dimboost.js

AD layer 0.7, Galaxy: costs 80 + 60g eighth dimensions (plus g^2 + g after 100 galaxies), resets boosts and makes tickspeed stronger. Sacrifice: (log10(sacrificed)/10)^2 on the 8th dimension, unlocked after 5 boosts. Source: galaxy.js, sacrifice.js

AD layer 1, Infinity: forced at 2^1024. The pre-break wall stops production and hides the UI except the Crunch button, and pays exactly 1 IP times multipliers. After Break Infinity: IP = 10^(log10(AM)/308 - 0.75). Source: game.js, antimatter-dimension.js tick

AD layer 2, Eternity: EP = 5^(log10(IP)/308 - 0.7). Layer 3, Reality: RM = 1000^(log10(EP)/4000 - 1), needs 1e4000 EP, with a linear patch for 1 to 10 RM. Each layer is a log of the one below. Source: game.js, machines.js

CH layer 1, Ascension (unlocks at Amenhotep level 150): hero souls = floor(heroLevels/2000) + primal souls floor(((z-80)/25)^1.3). Unspent hero souls give +10% DPS each. They are spent on ancients with per-level costs of n, n^1.5 or 1, and respec refunds 75%. Source: Hero_Souls, Ascension, Formulas, Ancients wikis

CH layer 2, Transcendence (after zone 300): AS = floor(5*log10(total HS)). Transcendent Power = 25 - 23*e^(-0.0003*AS) % multiplies primal hero souls, exponentially in zone. Outsiders: Xyliqil x1.5^level idle effectiveness, Chor'gorloth -(1-0.95^level) ancient cost, Phandoryss +100% DPS per level, Ponyboy +1000*level^2 % primal souls. Source: Ancient_Souls, Transcendence wikis
RG layer 1, Abdication (any time): gems from n(n+1)*5e11 coins, about sqrt(c/5e11), each gem giving +2% production. Factions, gems, trophies and challenges are kept. Source: Gems, Abdication wikis

RG layer 2, Reincarnation: first at 1e27 gems, x1000 each time, all gems reset. Reincarnation Power perks scale linearly or by power law in R: +50%*R production, +500%*R offline, R^1.75*t^0.65 % from R10. New features unlock at fixed R thresholds (R16 unique buildings, R22 neutral, R28 prestige, R90 research slot). Source: Reincarnation, Buildings wikis
RG layer 3, Ascension at R39, R99, R159 and R219: a rescale where building ratio goes 1.15 to 1.03 and every multiplier m becomes m^(1/10). Source: Ascension wiki

Pecorella comparison: a sqrt prestige (RG) needs 4x earnings to double. A cube root (Cookie Clicker) needs 8x. Egg, Inc. at ^0.14 needs about 128-141x. AdCap 150*sqrt(lifetime/1e15) lets players reset repeatedly at the same point for shrinking gains, while RG's max-based formula gives nothing for a repeat. Source: gamedeveloper.com part III

None of the three games can soft-lock. AD's free tier 1 production always reaches the next boost or galaxy. CH's failed boss drops the player back to farm, and a floor of 1 hero soul per 2000 hero levels always exists. RG allows abdication at any time, even with no gain. Sources: dimboost.js and galaxy.js, Formulas and Hero_Souls wikis, Abdication wiki
lessonsForToKin: Typing ladder (D3): model it as cost_L = C0 * r^(L-1) and tokens/press = 2^(L-1), so presses per level = C0 * (r/2)^(L-1). Recommended placeholder: C0 = 10, r = 3, cap at L10. That is 1,133 presses, about 4 min at 5 keys/s. Optionally raise r to 4 for the last 2 levels before the cap so the wall feels heavy. Avoid r = 2: every level then costs the same presses and growth runs away. Avoid r = 4 throughout: about 34 min of mashing is too long for an opening. Dev-panel knobs: C0, r, cap level and an optional late r.

Ladder cap and first net (D19): copy AD's pre-break Infinity wall, which stops antimatter at 1.79e308 and leaves one obvious button that always pays a fixed 1 IP. At the first computer's limit, ladder levels stop but presses keep paying tokens at the capped rate. Price the first net's design and code at about 2 to 3 min of capped typing (with 2^9 = 512 tokens/press at L10, that is roughly 300k to 450k tokens at 5 keys/s). The wall is then a signpost, not a block.

Copy costs (D5): use geometric pricing copy_n = B * g^n with g = 1.10 as the placeholder. CH heroes use 1.07, AdCap 1.07, RG buildings 1.15. With B = 100 and 1e6 tokens that buys 72 copies at 1.10, against 96 at 1.07 and 52 at 1.15. MIPS demand per copy (D11/D16) is a second limiter, so the token ratio can stay gentle. Use Pecorella's closed forms for 'buy max' (floor(log_g(c(g-1)/(B g^k) + 1))) and for bulk cost. Add AD/AdCap-style milestone multipliers: x2 copy output at 10, 25 and 50 copies (AD doubles per 10 bought, AdCap at 25 and 50, CH x4 per 25 levels). Distill perks can flatten g later, the way RG Ascension cuts 1.15 to 1.03.

Dedup event (D5): frame it like an AD Dimension Boost, as a gate that pays rather than a pure tax. When a net reaches its repeat threshold (placeholder: 20 copies, then +15 per later dedup, mirroring AD's 20 + 15*(boosts-5)), new copies add diminishing output until the player pays the dedup token cost. Paying restores full output and grants a permanent x2 on that net (DimBoost power 2). A player who ignores it keeps earning, just less, so there is no soft lock.

Gig money (D6): tie pay to progress the way CH ties gold to zone. In CH, gold grows x1.15 per zone, HP x1.145 and hero cost x1.07 per level, which works out to about 2 levels per zone. Make the next gig tier's pay grow slightly faster than the next hardware tier's price, for example pay x1.15 per gig tier against hardware x1.12 per MIPS step. That way gigs fund hardware a little faster than hardware gets expensive. Give deadlines the CH boss-timer shape: a fixed base (for example 60 s of real work) that tightens slowly with tier. A missed deadline pays part of the fee or drops the player to a smaller gig. Always keep one evergreen low gig (newspaper copy) so money never sits at zero.

Hardware compute (D11, D15, D16): AD tickspeed is the template for MIPS upgrades. One global multiplier on every job: price x10 per step for x1.1245 speed (6 steps is about x2). Add rare big purchases (a new machine or chip) that make every later small MIPS step stronger, the way AD galaxies do. Because oversubscribed jobs run at (capacity/demand)^2, each MIPS buy also removes part of the idle penalty. Show the player the effective-throughput gain, not just the raw MIPS. Dev-panel knobs: base cost, price ratio, MIPS multiplier per step, big-jump bonus.

Pipelines (D8): reward balance, following RG Druid Grand Balance, which boosts the least productive building by 0.25*(x*y*z/729)^0.9 of the three most built. Add a 'bottleneck bonus' to the slowest converter when the stages are within some ratio of each other. Active managers earn it and idle players get a scheduler later. For surplus specialised tokens, add an RG Royal Exchange-style sink: +10% additive to all nets per exchange, cost floor(20 * 1.1^x). Later 'nets that make data or nets' chains can use AD's cascade (tier n+1 feeds tier n at 1/10 rate), which gives polynomial growth that is cheap to simulate in both the browser and the pane.

Publishing events (D10, D20): use RG's approach of one seeded pseudorandom stream per event type ('market catches up', 'rival adopts your method', 'bad synthetic data'), with the stream state stored in the save. Reloads and switching between the browser and the Claude Code pane then cannot re-roll outcomes, and both hosts compute the same sequence. Space events with a randomised timer (Cookie Clicker style; RG Green Fingers fires every 30 s with randRange(1,2500) x production) at a few minutes apart, and cap the total cost per paper so publishing always nets positive. A simple, idle-safe positive counterpart: an Elven-Luck-style 1% chance per press of a burst worth some seconds of production.

Distill (D23): use a square-root prestige like RG gems, with a guaranteed floor like AD and CH. Placeholder: Distill points = max(1, floor(sqrt(lifetimeTokensThisRun / T0))), with T0 tuned so the first Distill shortly after the first AI paper gives about 3 to 10 points. Doubling the reward then takes 4x the tokens (cube root, Cookie Clicker style, needs 8x and is too harsh for an early layer). Base it on the run's max or lifetime as RG does, so a repeat reset at the same point gives nothing new. Let unspent points boost output (CH: +10% DPS per unspent hero soul) so banking is never wrong. Spend points on perks with mixed cost curves (CH ancients cost n, n^1.5 or flat 1 per level). Any later second layer can use CH's floor(5*log10(points)), which gives +5 per 10x.

Distill unlock and soft-lock safety (D23): the timer after the first AI paper is a deterministic threshold, like AD's boost and galaxy gates, not a random event. Every reset must leave typing at 1 token per press plus permanent perks, so the next run can always rebuild. RG lets players abdicate at any time even with no gain, and toKin can allow a zero-gain Distill after unlock behind a confirm prompt.

Active vs idle balance: offer an AD-style three-way exclusive choice in the research tree. 'Flow' decays with time since the last streak break (CH Juggernaut stacks with a 280 s grace and 5%/s decay). 'Batch' is a flat multiplier. 'Overnight' grows as a power of time since the last press (sqrt or ^0.65, like AD TS123 sqrt(1.39 t) or RG R10 t^0.65). Tune the crossovers the way AD does (active wins under about 2 min, idle wins after about 4.5 min). Use CH's idle-state rule: idle bonuses start after 60 s without presses and drop on 2 presses within 5 min. Keep presses worth something after nets arrive: each press gives tokens plus a share of a second of net output (CH caps clicks at 3.5% of DPS, RG Elf adds 50% of production per click, RG assistants give 5% of click per second). Placeholder: 2 to 5% per press, which at 5 keys/s is roughly a 1.1 to 1.25x boost for active players. Add short active buffs on a meter (RG mana: 1000 cap, 1/s, 200-mana Tax Collection gives 30 s of production) for a target of about 1.5 to 3x active over idle per hour, not 10x.

Automation is earned (D17): AD autobuyers start at 500 to 1200 ms intervals. Each upgrade multiplies the interval by 0.6 for 2x the cost in prestige currency, down to 100 ms. Price toKin's scheduler node and later auto-queue upgrades the same way, so idle players climb toward active throughput over several Distills rather than all at once.

Dev panel: expose every constant above as a live knob (ladder C0/r/cap, copy B/g/milestones, dedup threshold and increment, gig pay ratio and deadline, MIPS price ratio and step multiplier, pipeline balance exponent, event interval and size, Distill T0 and exponent, active/idle crossover times). Show the derived numbers next to them: presses per level, time to cap, copies affordable at the current pool, time to first Distill, and Distill points against tokens. All of these have closed forms, listed in the curves above.
