curves.name: AutoClipper cost and output
curves.formula: The first one costs $5. After that, cost = 1.1^n + 5, where n = owned. Output = n * clipperBoost clips/s: clipClick(clipperBoost*n/100) runs every 10 ms. clipperBoost rises by +0.25, +0.50 and +0.75 from projects that cost 750, 2,500 and 5,000 ops.
curves.purpose: The +5 constant keeps the first ~15 purchases nearly flat ($6.10, $6.61, $7.59 at n=10, $11.73 at n=20), then the exponential takes over ($50 at 40, $1,277 at 75).
curves.parameters: base 1.1, additive 5, tick 10 ms

curves.name: MegaClipper cost
curves.formula: The first costs 500 (globals.js). After that, cost = 1000 * 1.07^n. Output = 500 clips/s each * megaClipperBoost, from clipClick(megaClipperBoost*n*5) every 10 ms.
curves.purpose: A second-tier producer with a gentler ratio (1.07) and a much higher base: 1,070 / 1,967 / 5,427 / 29,457 at n = 1 / 10 / 25 / 50.
curves.parameters: base 1000, ratio 1.07

curves.name: Demand and sales (player-set price)
curves.formula: demand = (0.8 / price) * 1.1^(marketingLvl-1) * marketingEffectiveness * demandBoost * (1 + prestigeU/10). The UI shows it as demand*10 %. Every 100 ms, with probability demand/100, it sells floor(0.7 * demand^1.15) clips at price.
curves.purpose: The price knob. Derived: while demand < 100, revenue/s ~ 0.07 * d^2.15 * p, which goes as p^-1.15. A lower price always earns more until inventory runs out, so the best price is the highest one that still clears production. At marketing level 1: $0.25 gives 32% demand and ~0.6 clips/s; $0.10 gives 80% and ~5.6/s; $0.05 gives 160% and ~25.6/s; $0.03 gives ~80/s.
curves.parameters: 0.8 demand constant, 1.1 per marketing level, exponent 1.15, 100 ms tick
curves.source: https://www.decisionproblem.com/paperclips/main.js L4313-4315 (demand), L4564-4599 (sales loop), L3163 (display); numbers computed from these

curves.name: Marketing
curves.formula: adCost starts at 100 and doubles per level (100, 200, 400, 800...). Each level multiplies demand by 1.1.
curves.purpose: A cost-doubling upgrade with a small multiplicative payoff. It works because the price knob turns extra demand into revenue.
curves.parameters: cost x2, effect x1.1

curves.name: Wire market price
curves.formula: Shown price = ceil(base + 6*sin(k)). k increments with a 1.5% chance per 100 ms tick, so about every 6.7 s. Each spool bought adds +0.05 to base. Base decays by base/1000 every 250 ticks (25 s) without a purchase, while base > 15. Start values: base 20, spool 1,000 inches. Projects multiply the spool by 1.5, 1.75, 2, 3 and 11.
curves.purpose: An input cost the player can time: buying at the sine trough (~14) instead of the peak (~26) roughly halves the cost. Demand pressure (+0.05 per buy) and slow recovery act as a soft market response.
curves.parameters: amplitude 6, update chance 0.015/tick, +0.05 per buy, -0.1% per 25 s, floor 15

curves.name: WireBuyer automation
curves.formula: Buys one spool whenever wire <= 1, at whatever the current price is. It costs 7,000 ops.
curves.purpose: Automation that never stalls but never times the market. An attentive player beats it.
curves.parameters: trigger wire <= 1

curves.name: Trust thresholds (Fibonacci)
curves.formula: Trust goes up by 1 when clips >= nextTrust. nextTrust = Fibonacci * 1000: 3,000, 5,000, 8,000, 13,000, 21,000, 34,000, 55,000, 89,000... Each Trust buys +1 processor or +1 memory.
curves.purpose: Capacity unlocks spaced by ~x1.618. The player chooses between rate (processors) and cap (memory).

curves.name: Operations: rate and cap
curves.formula: Every 10 ms, ops += processors/10, so 10*processors ops/s, capped at memory*1000. Quantum ops above the cap go to tempOps, which decays at an accelerating rate (opFade grows by 3^3.5/1000 per tick after a delay).
curves.purpose: Memory caps the largest single purchase, because projects cost up to memory*1000 ops. Processors set the refill rate.
curves.parameters: 10 ops/s per processor, 1,000 ops per memory

curves.name: Creativity (pays only at cap)
curves.formula: Accrues only while operations are at the cap. speed = log10(P)*P^1.1 + P - 1, where P = processors; it starts at 1. Creativity +1 every 400/speed ticks of 10 ms, which is speed/4 per second. P=2 gives 0.41/s, P=10 gives 5.4/s, P=50 gives 43.7/s. The Creativity project (1,000 ops) appears when ops >= memory*1000.
curves.purpose: Turns a full cap into a second currency, so idling at the cap is productive. Hitting the cap is also the unlock trigger.
curves.parameters: threshold 400, 10 ms tick

curves.name: Quantum computing clicks
curves.formula: chip_i = sin(t*seed_i), with t += 1 per second and seeds 0.1, 0.2 ... 1.0. A click on Compute gives ceil(360 * sum(chip_i)) ops, which can be negative. Chips cost 10,000 ops plus 5,000 more each.
curves.purpose: A timing skill that rewards attention: click when the sum is high. Bad timing costs ops.
curves.parameters: 360 ops per unit of sine sum

curves.name: Anti-soft-lock project 'Beg for More Wire'
curves.formula: Trigger: portfolio < wireCost AND funds < wireCost AND wire < 1 AND unsoldClips < 1. Cost: 1 Trust, allowed down to -100. Gives one spool. Repeatable.
curves.purpose: An explicit escape valve from a dead state.

curves.name: Phase-2 costs: polynomial and declining ratio
curves.formula: Harvester and wire drone cost 1e6*(n+1)^2.25. Solar farm costs 1e8*(n+1)^2.78. Battery costs 1e7*(n+1)^2.54. Each clip factory multiplies the next price by x(11-n) for n=1..7, x2 for n=8-12, x1.5 for 13-19, x1.25 for 20-38, x1.15 for 39-78 and x1.10 after that.
curves.purpose: Polynomial costs keep mass-produced units readable. A falling ratio makes the first few factories dear and later ones relatively cheap.

curves.name: Power shortfall and momentum
curves.formula: If supply >= demand, the surplus fills batteries (10,000 each), performance stays >= 1, and with momentum performance += 0.0005 per tick. If short, batteries cover the gap first; after that, performance = supply/demand, which is linear.
curves.purpose: Oversubscription penalty with a buffer, plus a bonus for staying balanced.
curves.parameters: farm 50 and factory 200 power units

curves.name: Swarm disorganisation and boredom meters
curves.formula: ratio = max(H+1, W+1) / min(H+1, W+1). If ratio > 1.5, disorg += min(0.01, ratio/10000) per tick; if ratio < 1.5, disorg -= 0.01. At 100 the swarm is disorganised; Synchronize fixes it for 5,000 yomi. Boredom goes +1 per tick with no matter and -1 otherwise; at 30,000 the swarm is bored; Entertain fixes it for 10,000 creativity.
curves.purpose: Imbalance penalties that build slowly, visibly and reversibly before an event fires.
curves.parameters: threshold 100 and 30,000

curves.name: Investment engine
curves.formula: Every 2.5 s, each stock moves with 60% chance. It moves up with probability stockGainThreshold (0.5 + 0.01 per upgrade), by delta = ceil(rand*price / (4*riskiness)). Riskiness is 7, 5 or 1 for low, med or high. An upgrade costs floor((lvl+1)^e * 100) yomi.
curves.purpose: A random walk with a small, buyable positive drift.

curves.name: Building price and ratio reduction
curves.formula: price = base * r_eff^owned * (1 - LDR(discount, 1)), where r_eff = r + LDR(sum of ratio reductions, r - 1). Base ratios: field 1.12 (10 catnip), hut 2.5 (5 wood), log house, library, warehouse and smelter 1.15, barn 1.75 (50 wood), observatory and biolab 1.10, steamworks and magneto 1.25.
curves.purpose: 1.12-1.15 for producers, steep ratios for capacity (housing 2.5, barn 1.75). Ratio cuts saturate before r reaches 1. Hut costs run 5, 12, 31, 78, 195, 488, 1,221.

curves.name: Limited diminishing returns (getLimitedDR)
curves.formula: For x <= 0.75L the result is x. Above that, result = 0.75L + (1 - 0.25L / (x - 0.75L + 0.25L)) * 0.25L, which approaches L. With L=1: 1 gives 0.875, 2 gives 0.958, 10 gives 0.993.
curves.purpose: A soft cap on bonuses: linear at first, never reaching the limit.
curves.parameters: 75% undiminished

curves.name: Unlimited diminishing returns (triangular)
curves.formula: getUnlimitedDR(v, stripe) = (sqrt(1 + 8v/stripe) - 1) / 2. Karma uses stripe 5: 5 gives 1, 15 gives 2, 30 gives 3, 100 gives 5.84, 500 gives 13.65.
curves.purpose: Each further point costs linearly more input: the inverse of triangular numbers.
curves.parameters: stripe 5

curves.name: Storage caps
curves.formula: Each barn adds +5,000 catnip, +200 wood, +250 minerals, +60 coal and +50 iron. Each warehouse adds +150 wood and +200 minerals. addRes clamps to max(previous value, maxValue): new production at the cap is lost, but stock already over the cap stays. Crafted goods (beam, slab, parchment...) have no '<name>Max' effect, so they are uncapped.
curves.purpose: Raw resources are capped. Crafting into higher tiers is how players bank past the cap.

curves.name: Converter with partial run (smelter)
curves.formula: Each smelter takes 0.05 wood + 0.1 minerals per tick and makes 0.02 iron per tick. When inputs are short, run fraction = min over inputs of (available / needed), so output scales linearly.
curves.purpose: A converter that degrades gracefully when starved.
curves.parameters: 5 ticks/s

curves.name: Craft chain (conversion pipeline)
curves.formula: parchment = 175 furs. manuscript = 25 parchment + 400 culture. compendium = 55 manuscript + 9,000 science. blueprint = 25 compendium + 25,000 science. Also beam = 175 wood, slab = 250 minerals, plate = 125 iron, steel = 100 coal + 100 iron.
curves.purpose: Large lossy ratios, with a second input added at each tier. A close analogue of raw, prose and research tokens.

curves.name: Seasons and weather
curves.formula: Catnip multiplier is x1.5 in spring, x1.0 in summer and autumn, x0.25 in winter. From year 4, each season rolls 17.5% warm (+0.15) and 17.5% cold (-0.15). One day = 10 ticks = 2 s; a season is 100 days (200 s); a year is 800 s.
curves.purpose: A predictable cycle with a random modifier. Winter is the early pacing wall.
curves.parameters: ticksPerSecond 5
curves.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nuclear-unicorn/kittensgame/master/js/calendar.js L8-45, L217-218, L925-950, L1167-1182; game.js L2289

curves.name: Village upkeep, jobs and happiness
curves.formula: Each kitten eats 0.85 catnip/tick (4.25/s). Per tick: field 0.125 catnip, farmer 1 catnip, woodcutter 0.018 wood, scholar 0.035 science, miner 0.05 minerals, hunter 0.06 manpower. happiness = 100 - 2*(kittens - 5) + bonuses, with a floor of 25%. A festival adds +30%. Starvation: at most 1 kitten dies per 5 s while catnip is in deficit.
curves.purpose: A per-unit upkeep and crowding penalty, with a floor.

curves.name: Astronomical events and meteors
curves.formula: Astro event: 0.25% chance per day, mean gap 13.3 min. The Observe button lasts 300 ticks (60 s). If missed, the reward still comes with probability autoChance, set by observatories (SETI makes it 100%). Reward: 25 science * celestial bonus plus 1 starchart. Meteor: 0.1% per day (mean 33 min), auto-adds 50 + 25*mineralsRatio minerals. Offline: events = round(days * chance * autoChance).
curves.purpose: A clickable windfall. Absence only forfeits the upside, and automation buys it back.

curves.name: Offline catch-up (redshift)
curves.formula: 1 day per 2 s away, at full production rate. The cap is 10 game years (4,000 days, ~2.2 h); it becomes 40 years (~8.9 h) after year 1000 or once the player has paragon. Negative catnip is skipped offline. Caps are relaxed during catch-up and enforced afterwards. Temporal flux accrues at 5 per minute away and converts to 1 bonus second per 5 flux, which is 1 s per minute away, up to the flux cap.
curves.purpose: Absence pays the idle rate and never applies deficits.

curves.name: Reset: karma and paragon
curves.formula: karmaKittens = (k-35) + 3(k-60) + 4(k-100) + 5(k-150) + 10(k-300) + 15(k-750), counting each term only when positive. karma = UnlimitedDR(karmaKittens, 5). paragon = k - 70 when k > 70. Paragon production bonus = LDR(0.01*paragon, 2): +1% each, approaching +200%. Examples: 70 kittens give karma 4.62 and 0 paragon; 100 give 8.12 and 30; 150 give 14.81 and 80.
curves.purpose: Prestige pays nothing below a threshold, then grows with tiered marginal rates and diminishing returns.

curves.name: Linear building costs
curves.formula: Trap costs 10 + 10n wood (max 10). Hut costs 100 + 50n wood (max 20, 4 people each). Cart costs 30 wood (max 1). Lodge costs 200 wood + 10 fur + 5 meat.
curves.purpose: Linear costs with hard maximums instead of exponential ratios.

curves.name: Worker converters (10 s batches)
curves.formula: Every 10 s, multiplied by worker count: gatherer +1 wood; hunter +0.5 fur +0.5 meat; trapper -1 meat +1 bait; tanner -5 fur +1 leather; charcutier -5 meat -5 wood +1 cured meat; iron, coal and sulphur miners -1 cured meat +1 ore; steelworker -1 iron -1 coal +1 steel; armourer -1 steel -1 sulphur +1 bullets. All-or-nothing: if any input would go negative, the whole batch for that worker type is skipped.
curves.purpose: A multi-stage conversion chain managed by job allocation.
curves.parameters: delay 10 s

curves.name: Manual gathering, fire and builder automation
curves.formula: Gather wood gives +10 (+50 with a cart). The fire drops one step every 5 min. Stoking costs 1 wood with a 10 s cooldown. Once the builder is level 4 or higher, she stokes automatically when the fire is at flickering or below. Builder income is 2 wood per 10 s.
curves.purpose: A manual chore that later automates to 'good enough', not to the maximum.

curves.name: Random event scheduler
curves.formula: Next event in floor(rand*3) + 3 minutes, so 3, 4 or 5 minutes, mean 4. The event is picked uniformly from those whose isAvailable() is true. If none are valid, it retries after half that time. Only one event is active at a time, and the tab title blinks '*** EVENT ***'.
curves.purpose: Pacing for narrative events, gated by conditions.
curves.parameters: _EVENT_TIME_RANGE [3,6]

curves.name: Population arrivals
curves.formula: Arrivals every floor(rand*2.5) + 0.5 minutes, so 0.5, 1.5 or 2.5. Count = floor(rand*space/2 + space/2): between half and all of the free housing.
curves.purpose: Housing is the cap; arrivals fill it in lumps.
curves.parameters: _POP_DELAY [0.5,3], _HUT_ROOM 4

curves.name: Thieves (hoarding soft cap)
curves.formula: Once any store exceeds 5,000 and the world map is unlocked, thieves take 10 wood, 5 fur and 5 meat every 10 s until the Thief event fires. The player then chooses: hang him and get all stolen goods back, or spare him and get a permanent 'stealthy' perk.
curves.purpose: A drain triggered by stockpiling, resolved by a refund-or-perk choice.

curves.name: Mysterious Wanderer gamble
curves.formula: Give 100 wood: 50% chance that 300 wood comes back after 60 s, an expected value of +50%. Give 500 wood: 30% chance of 1,500, an expected value of -10%.
curves.purpose: An opt-in risk event: the small bet is good, the big bet is greedy.

curves.name: Storage priced as a share of the cap
curves.formula: A barn, shed or forge doubles the cap (increase.by = 2). Cost = floor(0.25 * current max * 2^(purchased - owned)). The base cap is 500. The Barn unlocks at 350 food (70% of the cap).
curves.purpose: Storage is always affordable once the stockpile reaches 25%, so caps can never soft-lock.
curves.parameters: costModifier 0.25

curves.name: Factory lines assigned by the player
curves.formula: Per line per second at tier 0, with tiers 1-4 scaling inputs and outputs by x1.5, x2, x2.5 and x3: alloy = 0.75 copper + 1 aluminium -> 0.075; polymer = 0.18 oil + 15 lumber -> 0.125; nano tube = 8 coal + 0.05 neutronium -> 0.2; furs = 10 money + 1.5 polymer -> 1. Lines are moved between recipes with +/- buttons.
curves.purpose: Pipeline management as slot allocation. Tech raises throughput and keeps the ratio.

curves.name: Generator chain
curves.formula: Base costs: 10, 100, 1e4, 1e6, 1e9, 1e13, 1e18, 1e24. Cost multiplier per 10 bought: 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e8, 1e10, 1e12, 1e15. Every 10 bought doubles production. Each dimension produces the previous one.
curves.purpose: A tiered chain where higher tiers feed lower tiers, giving polynomial-in-time growth.

curves.name: Three-stage pipeline
curves.formula: shaft -> elevator -> warehouse; throughput is effectively the minimum of the three stage rates. A manager makes a stage run without taps. Manager tier boosts reported for 2019: Junior x2 mining, x3 movement, -30% cost; Senior x4, x5, -50%; Executive x7, x7, -70%. Durations and cooldowns unknown.
curves.purpose: Bottleneck balancing. Guides advise keeping the elevator about 10 levels ahead of the warehouse.
curves.source: https://www.bluestacks.com/blog/game-guides/idle-miner-tycoon/idt-beginner-guide-en.html (stage sync, managers automate); tier numbers and the min() rule are unconfirmed

curves.name: Golden cookie spawn timer
curves.formula: Each frame at 30 fps: time++, then spawn if rand < ((time - Tmin) / (Tmax - Tmin))^5. Tmin = 5 min, Tmax = 15 min. Lifetime 13 s. Lucky day and Serendipity each halve Tmin and Tmax and double the lifetime. Derived: mean 7.44 min, median 7.48, 80% of spawns between 6.8 and 8.0 min. The same formula checked once per second gives a mean of 9.3 min.
curves.purpose: A pseudorandom windfall with a guaranteed quiet period and a rising hazard.
curves.parameters: exponent 5

curves.name: Offline production
curves.formula: Needs Twin Gates. Up to maxTime (1 h, doubled by each of 7 demon upgrades) at percent = 5% (+10% per angel upgrade, and more). Time beyond maxTime earns at 1/10 of that rate.
curves.purpose: Offline pays a small share of the online rate, with steep falloff after a cap.

curves.name: Silos (offline cap)
curves.formula: Each silo holds 1 h of away earnings. The Silo Capacity epic research adds 6 min per level, 20 levels, for +2 h. The standard permit allows 2 silos at half the online rate; the pro permit allows 10 silos at the full rate.
curves.purpose: An offline cap the player can buy up.
curves.source: https://egg-inc.fandom.com/wiki/Grain_Silo (seen only in a search excerpt; direct fetch returned HTTP 402)

curves.name: Generic cost and prestige
curves.formula: cost_next = base * rate^owned (Lemonade Stand: rate 1.07, base 4, 1.67/s). Prestige currency goes roughly as sqrt(earnings), so doubling it takes about 3-4x the earnings.
curves.purpose: The reference model: exponential cost against linear or polynomial production.

curves.name: Idle and active ancients
curves.formula: Siyalatas gives +25% DPS per level while the player is not clicking. Libertas gives an idle gold bonus (+25% per level per the wiki table). The idle threshold is reported as 60 s.
curves.purpose: Separate multipliers for idle and active builds.
curves.source: https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Libertas,_Ancient_of_Freedom (seen only in a search excerpt; the 60 s threshold is unconfirmed)

events: Cookie Clicker golden cookie: no spawn for 5 min, then a per-frame hazard of ((t-5)/(15-5))^5 at 30 fps. In practice it spawns at 6.8-8.0 min (80% band), mean 7.4 min, and stays on screen 13 s. The per-frame form depends on frame rate: checked once per second, the mean becomes 9.3 min. (orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js L5497-5503, L5934-5990)

Kittens astronomical event: 0.25%/day with 2 s days, mean 13.3 min, 60 s Observe window. A missed event still pays with the observatory autoChance. Meteors: 0.1%/day (mean 33 min), fully automatic. Offline events = round(days * chance * autoChance). (kittensgame js/calendar.js L250-300, L515-600, L730-760)
Kittens weather: a roll each season from year 4: 17.5% warm (+15% catnip), 17.5% cold (-15%). This is a seasonal modifier, not a click event. (calendar.js L925-950, L1178-1182)

A Dark Room scheduler: the next event comes in 3, 4 or 5 minutes (floor(rand*3)+3). It is picked uniformly from events whose conditions hold, retried at half time if none qualify, and only one runs at a time. (adarkroom script/events.js L6, L1313-1418)

A Dark Room condition-gated events: Noises and Mysterious Wanderer need wood; Hut Fire needs population > 50 and destroys 1 hut; Thief appears once any store > 5,000 after the map, draining 10 wood, 5 fur and 5 meat per 10 s until resolved with a refund-or-perk choice. (events/room.js, events/outside.js L69-95, events/global.js, room.js L874-877)
A Dark Room wanderer gamble: 100 wood gives a 50% chance of 300 back after 60 s; 500 wood gives a 30% chance of 1,500. (events/room.js L323-400)
Universal Paperclips wire market: the shown price moves with a 1.5% chance per 100 ms (~6.7 s) along ceil(base + 6*sin(k)). Base +0.05 per buy, -0.1% per 25 s idle, floor 15. (main.js L695-730)

Universal Paperclips swarm meters: disorganisation (drone ratio > 1.5, +min(0.01, ratio/10000)/tick, fires at 100) and boredom (+1/tick with no matter, fires at 30,000). Each has a paid fix: 5,000 yomi or 10,000 creativity. (main.js L2644-2700)
Universal Paperclips trust events: 'Production target met' at Fibonacci*1000 clips: 3k, 5k, 8k, 13k, 21k... (main.js L3370-3382)
Trimps Turkimp: a random-encounter buff to gather speed, x1.166 to x1.333 depending on talents. Seen in source only. (Trimps main.js L4177)
pacing: Producer price ratios cluster at 1.07-1.15: Paperclips AutoClipper 1.1 with a +5 constant, MegaClipper 1.07, Kittens producers 1.12-1.15, AdCap Lemonade 1.07. Capacity items are steeper: Kittens hut 2.5, barn 1.75; Paperclips marketing x2 per level.
Additive constants flatten the opening. Paperclips' 1.1^n + 5 stays under $8 for the first 10 AutoClippers and under $12 until 20.
Paperclips' clip-factory ratio falls with count (x10, x9 ... x4, then x2, x1.5, x1.25, x1.15, x1.10), and late units use polynomial costs ((n+1)^2.25 to ^2.78), so mass purchases stay readable.
Unlock thresholds can grow by the golden ratio (Paperclips Trust: 3k, 5k, 8k, 13k, 21k clips), a gentle ~x1.6 per step.
Kittens time units: tick 200 ms, day 2 s, season 200 s, year 800 s. Winter catnip x0.25 is the early wall that forces storage and farmer planning.

A Dark Room is minute-paced: events every 3-5 min, arrivals every 0.5-2.5 min, fire decays every 5 min, workers pay every 10 s. Costs are linear (+10 or +50 per unit) with hard maximums (10 traps, 20 huts).

Caps double as pacing gates. Paperclips ops cap = memory*1000 sets the most expensive project. Trimps storage costs 25% of the current cap and doubles it, and its Barn unlocks at 70% full. Kittens raw resources are capped while crafted goods are not.
Automation arrives late and pays 'never stall', not 'optimal': Paperclips WireBuyer (7,000 ops), AutoTourney (50,000 creativity), A Dark Room builder auto-stoke at flickering.
Generator chains (Antimatter Dimensions) grow costs much faster per tier (x1e3 to x1e15 per 10 bought). Each 10 bought doubles output, which keeps 'buy 10' as the natural unit.
prestige: Kittens: karmaKittens accrue only above 35 kittens, with marginal rates 1/3/4/5/10/15 above 35/60/100/150/300/750. karma = (sqrt(1 + 8*kk/5) - 1)/2. Paragon = kittens - 70 (only above 70) and gives +1% production each through LDR toward +200%. Examples: reset at 70 kittens gives karma 4.6 and paragon 0; at 100, 8.1 and 30; at 150, 14.8 and 80. (game.js L5466-5560, L5867-5897; prestige.js L557-568)

Universal Paperclips: at the end the player picks one of two flat, permanent bonuses: new universe, +10% demand per level (demand += demand/10 * prestigeU), or simulation, +10% creativity speed per level (ss = speed*(1 + prestigeS/10)). (main.js L4315, L3266-3272; projects.js L2142-2147)
Pecorella's model: prestige currency ~ sqrt(lifetime or max earnings), so doubling it needs ~3-4x the earnings of the previous run. (gamedeveloper.com 'The Math of Idle Games, Part III')
Kittens keeps the offline cap generous (40 years instead of 10) once the player has any paragon, so prestige also improves offline quality of life. (js/time.js L251-252)
A Dark Room has no prestige loop in the village, and Trimps and Antimatter Dimensions use layered resets. Both are out of scope for these numbers.
surveys.activeVsIdle: The surveyed games reward attention with upside that stays optional, and absence never costs the player anything. Universal Paperclips has no offline catch-up at all: main.js never reads the clock. While it runs, attention pays through price tuning (revenue goes as price^-1.15 until stock runs out, so the best price tracks capacity), wire-market timing (base plus or minus 6), quantum clicks (ceil(360*sum of sin(t*seed)), which can be negative), and tournament strategy picks. Automation (WireBuyer at 7,000 ops, AutoTourney at 50,000 creativity) keeps things from stalling but buys at any price. Kittens Game is the best model for absence. Offline time runs at the full production rate up to a cap (10 game years, about 2.2 h, rising to about 8.9 h after paragon). Negative catnip is skipped offline, so kittens never starve while away. Missed sky events pay at the automated observatory chance. Time past the cap is partly banked as temporal flux, 1 bonus second per minute away. Online, Kittens rewards the 60 s Observe button and season planning. Its harsh online penalty is starvation, at most 1 kitten per 5 s. A Dark Room has no offline progress; its builder auto-stokes the fire only to 'flickering' and its events wait for the player. Cookie Clicker pays offline at 5% for 1 h, then a tenth of that rate. Egg, Inc. buys offline time in 1 h silos (+6 min per research level), at half the online rate on the standard permit and full rate on the pro permit. Clicker Heroes splits multipliers between idle play (Siyalatas, Libertas) and active play. The shared pattern has four parts. (1) Idle and offline play earn a baseline set by automation. (2) Attention adds a bounded bonus through timing, tuning or catching events. (3) Negative effects are skipped or floored while the player is away. (4) The active edge comes from managing something (price, inputs, bottlenecks), not from raw clicking.
lessonsForToKin: Typing ladder (D3): tokens per press are 2^L and the cost to reach L+1 is c0*r^L, so presses per level are c0*(r/2)^L. With c0 = 10: r = 2 gives a flat 10 presses per level, which runs away. r = 3 gives 10, 15, 22.5, 34, 51, 76, 114, 171 presses: 493 to level 8, about 1.4 min at 6 keys/s. r = 4 gives 10, 20, 40 ... 1,280: 2,550 to level 8 (about 7 min) and 10,230 to level 10 (about 28 min). Recommended placeholder: r = 4 with the cap at level 8-9 (256-512 tokens per press), so the first machine's ceiling takes roughly 7-14 minutes of real typing. Expose c0, r and the cap level in the dev panel.

Typing cap as unlock trigger (D19): copy Paperclips' Creativity project, which appears when ops >= memory*1000 and then makes the full cap pay a second currency (speed/4 per s). When the ladder hits the first computer's limit, show 'Design a neural net' at once. Let presses at the cap keep paying something, for example 'notes' that discount net Design tokens, so typing at the cap is never wasted. Any overflow display should fade like Paperclips' tempOps rather than vanish.

Copy costs (D5): use base*r^n with r = 1.10 as the placeholder; the dev panel range is 1.07-1.15, matching Paperclips 1.07-1.1 and the Kittens producers. With base 20, 25 copies cost about 2.0k cumulative at 1.10 and 4.3k at 1.15. Copies also consume MIPS under (c/d)^2, so compute already limits copy count and the token ratio should not be steep as well. Route copy-cost research through Kittens' LDR: r_eff = r - LDR(reduction, r - 1), so the ratio approaches 1 and never reaches it. For hundreds of copies later, switch to Paperclips' polynomial form base*(n+1)^2.25 so numbers stay readable.

Dedup (D5): model repetition as a visible meter like Paperclips' disorganisation. It rises while copies outrun seed variety, falls when variety is restored, and fires the 'copies repeat' event at a threshold, with hysteresis so it does not flicker. A suggested formula (my own, not from any of these games): unique output = S*(1 - (1 - 1/S)^n) for S seeds. With S = 50, unique share is 91% at 10 copies, 83% at 20 and 64% at 50. Fire the event below about 80% unique share. Dedup costs tokens and doubles S. The data-cleaning technique (D9) makes dedup cheaper. Floor the penalty like Kittens' 25% happiness floor: never below 50% of nominal output.

Gig money and the price knob (D6): Paperclips shows that a player-set price drives demand of about k/price, with units sold growing as demand^1.15. Revenue then rises as price falls until capacity runs out, so the best price is the highest one that still fills capacity. Let the player set a rate per gig token: gig offers arrive at rate k/rate and deadline slack shrinks as the rate falls. Active players re-tune each time their token capacity changes; idle players can use an 'auto-price to capacity' unlock with a slight lag.

Publishing costs on gig pay (D10/D20): apply 'the market catches up' as a multiplier on the demand constant (for example x0.92 per event), not a flat cut. Let it recover slowly toward a floor, the way Paperclips' wire base decays 0.1% every 25 s with a floor of 15. Floor pay at 50% of the pre-publish level so publishing can never zero out income.

Gig deadlines (D6): follow Kittens' Observe window, which lasts 60 s and then auto-resolves at the automation chance. A missed deadline only forfeits the gig's bonus and never charges a penalty. While the player is away, gigs complete at the idle rate if their nets can do the work, or expire quietly.

Anti-soft-lock valve (Ground rules, D23): copy Paperclips' 'Beg for More Wire'. It appears only when wire < 1, funds < wire cost, no stock is left and the portfolio is below the wire cost, costs 1 Trust (allowed down to -100) and is repeatable. toKin keeps hand presses (D2) and adds an always-available fallback gig ('help the professor', paying enough for the cheapest needed hardware) that appears whenever money is below the cheapest useful purchase. Price any storage like Trimps, at 25% of the current cap, so it is always affordable once the stock is a quarter full.

Hardware, RAM and MIPS (D11/D15): mirror Paperclips' processors and memory. Memory caps the largest single purchase (ops cap = memory*1000) while processors set the rate (10 ops/s each). In toKin, RAM caps the largest net that can load and MIPS sets speed, and buying one or the other is a real choice. Hardware unlocks or tiers can be spaced by the golden ratio like Trust (3k, 5k, 8k, 13k...).

Oversubscription (D16): (c/d)^2 is harsher than anything surveyed. Paperclips power falls off linearly (performance = supply/demand), Kittens converters scale linearly to their inputs, and A Dark Room skips whole batches. Keep it as the idle penalty (3 jobs of 1 MIPS on a 2 MIPS machine give 1.33 MIPS of work oversubscribed against 2.0 queued), but borrow Paperclips' two cushions. First, a buffer like batteries, for example a small burst allowance that absorbs short spikes. Second, momentum: Paperclips adds +0.0005 per tick while fully supplied, so a perfectly queued machine could earn a small growing bonus.

Overclock crash (D15): A Dark Room's destructive Hut Fire only fires above 50 population and destroys one hut. Gate crash risk by how hard the player overclocks, and make the cost temporary (reboot downtime, lost in-flight training progress). Never delete purchased hardware.

Pipelines and converters (D8): use Kittens' partial-run rule, where a converter runs at min(available/needed) of its inputs, not A Dark Room's all-or-nothing batch, which idles downstream stages silently. Pipeline throughput is the minimum of its stage rates, as in Idle Miner Tycoon; always highlight the bottleneck stage, since spotting it is the active player's job.

Conversion ratios (D8/D9): Kittens' chain is steep and lossy (175:1, then 25:1 + 400 culture, 55:1 + 9,000 science, 25:1 + 25,000 science) and adds a second input at each tier. Placeholders: raw to prose 10:1; prose to research 5:1 plus raw or compute as a second feed. Present converter capacity as Evolve-style lines the player moves between recipes with +/-. Each tech tier scales a line's input and output together (x1.5, x2, x2.5, x3) and keeps the ratio.

Automation for idle players (D13/D17): price it late and make it 'never stalls, not optimal', like Paperclips' WireBuyer (7,000 ops, buys whenever wire runs out, at any price) and the Dark Room builder (stokes only to flickering). A pipeline auto-balancer keeps every stage running at a safe ratio, and active rebalancing should beat it by roughly 20-30%. This matches the scheduler node in D17.

Publishing events (D20): define the hazard per second, not per tick. Cookie Clicker's per-frame ((t-5)/(15-5))^5 gives a 7.4 min mean at 30 fps but 9.3 min if checked once a second. Use p_tick = 1 - exp(-h0*((t - min)/(max - min))^k * dt) so tick rate never changes pacing. Placeholders per paper: 'market catches up' at min 2 / max 8 min, k = 2 (mean about 3-4 min); 'a rival adopts your method' at min 5 / max 20 min. Expose min, max and k in the dev panel. Show at most one event at a time, as A Dark Room does, and retry at half time if none qualifies.

Make cost events into choices (D20): A Dark Room's Thief lets the player get the stolen goods back or take a permanent perk. For 'a rival adopts your method', offer to spend research or prose tokens to keep the edge (a refund) or accept the fade for a small permanent Citations boost (a perk). If the player is away, the event auto-resolves to the cheaper option, the way Kittens auto-observes at the automation chance; never to the worst one.

Data-gathering risk events (brainstorm): synthetic data can follow A Dark Room's Wanderer gamble (100 wood: 50% chance of 300; 500 wood: 30% chance of 1,500). A small synthetic batch has a good expected value and a big batch is greedy, with a chance the trained model comes out bad. Data-cleaning research lowers that chance. Scraping by hand stays safe but slow, as a no-risk floor.

Distill (D23): give nothing below a threshold, then grow, like Kittens (karma only above 35 kittens, paragon above 70). Unlock Distill a fixed time (placeholder 10 min) after the first AI paper. Distill points = floor(sqrt(Citations/c0)), so doubling them takes 4x the Citations (Pecorella), and the production bonus runs through LDR toward a cap, as paragon approaches +200%. Offer Paperclips' two-way pick at each Distill: +10% tokens ('speed') or +10% research ('insight').

Distill must never soft-lock the next run: keep only permanent multipliers, and make sure every first-run unlock (the first net at the typing cap, the first gig, the first paper) depends on things a reset restores at once, such as hand presses and the basic CPU. As Kittens does with paragon, let Distill also improve quality of life, for example a longer offline cap.

Active vs idle, offline (ground rule): use Kittens' redshift. Offline time runs at the idle rate, with the priority list and (c/d)^2 in force unless the scheduler node is researched, up to a cap: placeholder 2 h, extended by research the way Egg, Inc. silos add +6 min per level. Skip every negative effect offline (Kittens skips catnip deficits). Bank time past the cap as a small boost, like Kittens' 1 s per minute away. Avoid Cookie Clicker's 5%: it makes absence feel like loss.

Active vs idle, online upside: every attention mechanic should add upside and never punish an idle player. Candidates: (a) queuing jobs by hand to escape (c/d)^2; (b) timing gig rates or hardware buys against a sine-like market (Paperclips wire swings by plus or minus 6 around about 20); (c) a quantum-style timing button (sum of sines), for example 'inspiration', which pays ceil(K*sum) tokens and can go negative, so timing matters; (d) catching windfall events inside a 60 s window, with automation buying back part of the missed value.

curves.name: Next generator cost
curves.formula: cost_next = cost_base * rate_growth^owned
curves.purpose: Exponential cost against linear production makes the slowdown that drives purchase choices and prestige.
curves.parameters: AdCap Lemonade Stand: base 4 (3.738 effective), rate 1.07. With 10 owned the next one costs 4*1.07^10 = 7.87.

curves.name: Linear production
curves.formula: production_total = (production_base * owned) * multipliers
curves.purpose: Production grows linearly or polynomially. Exponential cost always overtakes it in the end, so the curve flattens.
curves.parameters: Lemonade 1.67/s base. x2 at 25 and at 50 owned, stacking. 10 owned gives 16.7/s.

curves.name: Bulk buy cost
curves.formula: cost(n) = b * r^k * (r^n - 1) / (r - 1)
curves.purpose: Closed form for buy x10, x100 and max buttons.
curves.parameters: b = base price, r = growth rate, k = owned, n = number to buy.

curves.name: Max affordable
curves.formula: max = floor( log( c*(r-1) / (b*r^k) + 1 ) / log(r) )
curves.purpose: The buy-max button. It holds only for a plain geometric cost with no shifting exponents.
curves.parameters: c = currency held.

curves.name: Generators that produce generators
curves.formula: A chain of n tiers grows as x^n/n!; with 4 tiers, total generators = 1 + t + t^2/2 + t^3/6. As tiers are added it approaches e^x (Taylor series).
curves.purpose: Polynomial growth on each tier that tends toward exponential. The model for 'nets that make nets'.
curves.parameters: Derivative Clicker High Schooler cost 5*1.1^n. Each Tier 1 building gives +0.05% to all Tier 1.

curves.name: Building price
curves.formula: price = ceil( basePrice * 1.15^max(0, amount - free) ); Game.priceIncrease = 1.15
curves.purpose: The standard 1.15 ratio. Price doubles about every 5 buys and is about x33 after 25.
curves.parameters: Cursor base price 15. Bulk buy is the plain sum of single prices, with no discount.

curves.name: Building base price and CpS by tier n
curves.formula: baseCps = ceil(n^(0.5n + 2) * 10)/10 (then rounded); basePrice = (n + 9 + (n<5 ? 0 : (n-5)^1.75 * 5)) * 10^n * max(1, n-14) (then rounded)
curves.purpose: Every tier costs about x11 to x16 more and makes about x5.5 to x8 more, so base payback grows each tier.
curves.parameters: Computed from the formula: Grandma 100/1, Farm 1100/8, Mine 12000/47, Factory 130000/260, Bank 1.4M/1400, Temple 20M/7800, Wizard 330M/44000. Payback in seconds: 100, 138, 255, 500, 1000, 2564, 7500, 19615 (about x1.4 to x2.9 a tier). The Cursor is 15 for 0.1/s, a 150 s payback.

curves.name: Sell refund
curves.formula: sell value = sum of past prices * 0.25 (x(1 + Earth Shatterer aura))
curves.purpose: Purchases can be undone at a loss. A safety valve against bad buys.
curves.parameters: giveBack = 0.25

curves.name: Prestige level (heavenly chips)
curves.formula: prestige = floor( (cookiesBakedAllTime / 1e12)^(1/3) ); inverse cookies = chips^3 * 1e12
curves.purpose: A cube-root prestige. Doubling it needs x8 lifetime cookies.
curves.parameters: HCfactor = 3. Level 1 at 1e12 and level 2 at 8e12. The wiki advises a first ascension at 365 chips, which is about 4.9e19 cookies.

curves.name: Prestige CpS bonus
curves.formula: mult += prestige * 0.01 * heavenlyPower * heavenlyMultiplier; the unlock upgrades give 5%, then +20% and +25% of the potential
curves.purpose: +1% CpS per prestige level, unlocked step by step inside each run.
curves.parameters: The Legacy text says 'permanent +1% CpS per level'.

curves.name: Golden cookie spawn hazard
curves.formula: every frame: time++; spawn if random() < ( max(0, (time - minTime)/(maxTime - minTime)) )^5; minTime = 5 min, maxTime = 15 min (times fps, times modifiers)
curves.purpose: A pseudorandom event that feels random but arrives on a fairly regular beat. The timer restarts when the cookie dies.
curves.parameters: fps = 30. Computed: mean 7.44 min, 10th to 90th percentile 6.81 to 8.03 min. With Lucky day and Serendipity (each halves the times) the mean is 2.02 min.
curves.source: https://orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js (lines 5497-5508, 5934-5992, fps at 2083); distribution computed in scratchpad

curves.name: Golden cookie lifetime
curves.formula: dur = 13 s (x2 Lucky day, x2 Serendipity, x0.95^(goldens on screen - 1))
curves.purpose: A short window that rewards attention: the active-play tax.
curves.parameters: 13 s base

curves.name: Golden and wrath cookie effects
curves.formula: Frenzy: x7 CpS for 77 s. Lucky: + min(cookies*0.15, CpS*60*15) + 13. Click frenzy: x777 click for 13 s (10% roll). Ruin (wrath): - min(cookies*0.05, CpS*60*10) + 13, capped at the bank. Clot (wrath): x0.5 CpS for 66 s. 80% chance to force a different effect than the last one.
curves.purpose: Positive and negative event payloads. Each is bounded by the smaller of a share of the bank and N minutes of production, so no event can wipe a player.
curves.parameters: Base pool: golden = [frenzy, multiply cookies]; wrath = [clot, multiply, ruin]. Building special 25% if 10 or more buildings.

curves.name: Manual click power track
curves.formula: Reinforced index finger 100, Carpal tunnel prevention cream 500, Ambidextrous 10,000: each doubles mouse and cursors. Each mouse upgrade (Plastic 50,000; Iron 5,000,000; ...) adds +1% of CpS per click.
curves.purpose: A doubling manual ladder, like toKin's typing ladder, then clicks that scale with idle CpS so clicking stays relevant.
curves.parameters: Price steps x5 then x20 for each x2 of click power.

curves.name: Click rate guard
curves.formula: Clicks are ignored if now - lastClick < 1000/50 ms (mouse) or 1000/3 ms when event.detail === 0 (keyboard-activated). Clicks under 1000/15 ms apart raise autoclickerDetected.
curves.purpose: Caps input rate and flags autoclickers. Key-activated clicks are held to 3 per second.
curves.parameters: 50/s mouse, 3/s keyboard, 15/s flag

curves.name: Offline production (Twin Gates of Transcendence)
curves.formula: offline rate = 5% of CpS for the first hour, then reduced by a further 90% to 0.5%. Fern tea adds +3%.
curves.purpose: Idle-while-closed is a bought prestige perk and pays far less than being present.
curves.parameters: 5% for up to 1 h, then 0.5%

curves.name: Business table
curves.formula: cost_n = initialCost * coefficient^(n-1); productivity = revenue / cycleTime
curves.purpose: A tiered generator set. Each tier costs x12. Cycle time goes x2 then x4. The per-item coefficient drops from 1.15 to 1.07 up the tiers.

curves.name: Cycle-time milestones
curves.formula: cycle time halves at 25, 50, 100, 200, 300 and 400 of a business, and halves again when ALL businesses reach each milestone; at most 12 halvings (1/4096)
curves.purpose: Ownership milestones as bumps and local victories against the exponential cost.
curves.parameters: Oil Company goes from 10 h 14 m to about 9 s at 400 of everything

curves.name: Angel investors (prestige)
curves.formula: angels = 150 * sqrt(lifetimeEarnings / 1e15) = sqrt(L / (400e9/9)) minus angels from earlier sessions, floored; each angel +2% profit, additive
curves.purpose: A square-root prestige. Doubling needs x4 lifetime earnings. Resetting at the same point still pays a little.
curves.parameters: First angel at about $44.4B lifetime; 150 angels at 1e15; 4,743 at 1e18. Angels can be sacrificed to buy upgrades, which loses their bonus.

curves.name: Manager (first automation) costs
curves.formula: flat price per business manager
curves.purpose: Managers restart cycles by themselves, online and offline. This is the switch from clicker to idle.
curves.parameters: Lemonade $1,000; Newspaper $15,000; Car Wash $100,000; Pizza $500,000; Donut $1.2M; Shrimp $10M; Hockey $111,111,111; Movie $555,555,555; Bank $10B; Oil $100B

curves.name: Hero level cost
curves.formula: cost = floor( floor(BaseCost * 1.07^Level) * CostReduction ); Ace Scouts use 1.22
curves.purpose: A 1.07 ratio on a single upgrade track per hero. About x2 every 10 levels and about x5.4 every 25.
curves.parameters: Treebeast base 50; level 114 to 115 costs 111,871.

curves.name: Hero DPS milestones and efficiency decay
curves.formula: DPS = Base * Static * Level * 4^((Level-200)/25) from level 200 (x10 at 1000..8000). Below 200: DPS/Cost proportional to Level * 1.07^-Level. Above 200: DPS/Cost proportional to e^(0.0555 L - 0.0677 L) = 0.988^L.
curves.purpose: Shows polynomial against exponential: by level 199 a hero is 0.03% as cost-efficient as at level 1. The x4 every 25 levels slows the decay to 1.2% a level.
curves.parameters: x4 per 25 levels; x5 for later heroes from 525 to 725

curves.name: Monster HP
curves.formula: Zones 1-140: ceil(10*(L - 1 + 1.55^(L-1)) * [boss x10]). Zones 141-500: ceil(10*(139 + 1.55^139 * 1.145^(L-140))). Zone 501 on: the per-zone factor grows by 0.001 every 500 zones.
curves.purpose: A demand curve with a deliberate change of ratio at zone 140 (1.55 to 1.145) to set where the wall sits.
curves.parameters: Gold worth x1.60255 per zone until 140, then 4.717e28 * 1.15^(L-140)

curves.name: Hero Souls (prestige)
curves.formula: souls = floor(totalHeroLevels / 2000) + primal boss souls floor(((zone - 80)/25)^1.3); each soul +10% DPS
curves.purpose: Prestige tied to ownership. In effect a log of the exponential progress.
curves.parameters: Primal boss chance 25% (falls 0.02 every 500 zones); 110, 120, 130 always primal; ascension unlocks at Amenhotep level 150; the wiki advises a first ascension at zone 130 or later.

curves.name: AutoClipper and MegaClipper costs
curves.formula: clipperCost = 1.1^clipmakerLevel + 5 (first one $5); megaClipperCost = 1.07^megaClipperLevel * 1000
curves.purpose: The '+5' keeps early AutoClippers nearly flat before the exponent takes over: a cheap first automation.
curves.parameters: Initial clipperCost 5

curves.name: Marketing cost
curves.formula: adCost = floor(adCost * 2) per level; marketing = 1.1^(marketingLvl - 1); demand = (0.8/margin) * marketing * effectiveness * boost
curves.purpose: A x2 cost ratio on a weak x1.1 effect. Steep on purpose, so research multipliers matter more.

curves.name: Trust milestones
curves.formula: trust +1 when clips >= nextTrust; nextTrust = fib(next) * 1000 (Fibonacci: 3000, 5000, 8000, 13000, ...)
curves.purpose: Milestones that grow slower than exponential ratios, spent on compute (processors or memory).
curves.parameters: Start 2 trust at 2000 clips

curves.name: Compute: processors, memory, creativity
curves.formula: Each 100 ms tick, ops += processors/10 until ops = memory*1000. When ops are full, creativity grows at log10(processors) * processors^1.1 + processors - 1.
curves.purpose: Compute split into speed (processors) and capacity (memory). A full buffer spills into a second resource instead of wasting idle time.
curves.parameters: 1000 ops per memory. The wiki warns that over 30 to 35 processors in stage 1 starves memory and can stall the run.

curves.name: Anti-soft-lock rescues
curves.formula: if (unsoldClips < 1 && funds < wireCost && wire < 1) unlock computing early; project 'Beg for More Wire' (1 Trust) triggers when out of wire, funds and clips, and grants 1 spool
curves.purpose: Detects the dead state explicitly and offers a way out.

curves.name: Dimension cost per 10
curves.formula: Buying 10 of a dimension gives x2 to it and multiplies its price by a per-tier factor. Past Infinity, the price multiplier itself rises x10 per purchase (super-exponential).
curves.purpose: Step costs in batches of 10, with milestone multipliers built into the batch.
curves.parameters: Base cost / per-10 multiplier: D1 10/1e3, D2 100/1e4, D3 1e4/1e5, D4 1e6/1e6, D5 1e9/1e8, D6 1e13/1e10, D7 1e18/1e12, D8 1e24/1e15. D1 makes 1 AM/s; each higher tier makes 0.1/s of the one below.

curves.name: Infinity and Eternity points (prestige)
curves.purpose: An extreme root (x10 IP per 1e308 AM) for nested prestige layers.
curves.parameters: First Infinity at 1.79e308 AM (2^1024)

curves.name: Building price ratios
curves.formula: price = basePrice * priceRatio^owned
curves.purpose: The ratio differs by role: 1.12 for basic food, 1.15 as default, 1.25 to 2.5 for capacity buildings.
curves.parameters: field 10 catnip at 1.12; most buildings 1.15; observatory 1.10; steamworks, magneto, ziggurat 1.25; brewery 1.5; barn and unicorn pasture 1.75; hut 2.5

curves.name: Unlimited diminishing returns (karma)
curves.formula: getUnlimitedDR(v, stripe) = ( sqrt(1 + 8*v/stripe) - 1 ) / 2; inverse = stripe/2 * p * (p+1)
curves.purpose: The triangular-number inverse prestige, the same shape as Realm Grinder. Doubling it needs about x3 to x4.
curves.parameters: karmaKittens = (k-35) + 3(k-60) + 4(k-100) + 5(k-150) + 10(k-300) + 15(k-750) for each threshold passed; stripe 5

curves.name: Limited diminishing returns
curves.formula: If effect <= 0.75*limit, no reduction. Otherwise 0.75*limit + (1 - d/(x + d)) * d, with d = 0.25*limit and x = effect - 0.75*limit.
curves.purpose: A soft cap on percentage bonuses that approaches the limit but never passes it.

curves.name: Crafting chain (pipeline)
curves.formula: craftedAmount = amt * (1 + craftRatio). parchment = 175 furs; manuscript = 25 parchment + 400 culture; compendium = 55 manuscript + 9000 science; blueprint = 25 compendium + 25000 science
curves.purpose: A multi-stage converter chain. Upgrades raise the output multiplier and leave input ratios alone.
curves.parameters: beam = 175 wood; slab = 250 minerals; plate = 125 iron

curves.name: Prestige (gems)
curves.formula: p = ( sqrt(1 + 8*c_M/1e12) - 1 ) / 2, the inverse of c_M = 1e12 * p(p+1)/2, based on MAX coins in a run
curves.purpose: Triangular prestige. Resetting at the same point gives nothing, so each run must beat the last.
curves.parameters: Doubling needs about x4 the previous run

curves.name: Prestige (soul eggs)
curves.formula: delta_p = (c_R / 1e6)^0.14 (earnings this run)
curves.purpose: A very flat root that forces long runs.
curves.parameters: Doubling needs 2^(1/0.14), about x141 (the article rounds to x128 = 2^7). Offline earning capped at 2 h.

curves.name: Upgrade cost growth
curves.formula: cost and reward grow at 1.1x per level (described as 11% to 19% over the previous upgrade); cost passes reward at about level 35
curves.purpose: A shipped data point. A 0.01 change in the ratio makes a large difference by the 20th upgrade, so tune in exponent space.

curves.name: Birthday problem and expected distinct outputs
curves.formula: P(any repeat) ~ 1 - e^(-k(k-1)/(2S)); expected distinct = S - S*((S-1)/S)^k; expected repeats = k - distinct
curves.purpose: Makes copy collisions emerge from the copy count instead of a fixed timer.
curves.parameters: Computed: S=50 gives 10 copies 59% chance of a repeat and 91% unique; 25 copies 79% unique; 50 copies 64%. S=200 gives 25 copies 78% chance of a repeat and 94% unique; 100 copies 79% unique.

curves.name: Oversubscription
curves.formula: per-job speed = min(1, c/d)^2; machine throughput = min(1, c/d)
curves.purpose: The idle penalty that active queueing removes.
curves.parameters: Computed: demand 1.25x gives 64% per job and 80% machine; 1.5x 44% and 67%; 2x 25% and 50%; 3x 11% and 33%; 4x 6% and 25%

curves.name: Typing ladder presses per level
curves.formula: tokens/press at level L = 2^L; cost of level L+1 = C0*r^L; presses to afford = C0*(r/2)^L; total presses to level N = C0*((r/2)^N - 1)/((r/2) - 1)
curves.purpose: Exponential production against exponential cost: the presses per level grow at r/2.
curves.parameters: C0 = 10, 8 levels, 5 presses/s: r=2 gives 80 presses (0.3 min); r=3 gives 493 (1.6 min), last level 171 presses; r=3.5 gives 1160 (3.9 min); r=4 gives 2550 (8.5 min).
curves.source: derived from D3; computed in scratchpad (no external source)

curves.name: MIPS by CPU
curves.formula: MIPS at clock and year
curves.purpose: A loose real-world compute ladder for hardware tiers. Each generation is about x2 to x4.

events: Cookie Clicker golden cookie spawn: after each cookie dies the timer resets. For each frame past minTime (5 min) the spawn chance is ((t - min)/(max - min))^5, which reaches certainty at maxTime (15 min). At 30 fps the mean is 7.44 min, with 80% of spawns between 6.8 and 8.0 min (computed). Each cookie stays 13 s on screen. Source: https://orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js lines 5497-5508, 5934-5992, 5607-5623.

Cookie Clicker effect selection: the golden base pool is [frenzy, multiply cookies]. Click frenzy is added on a 10% roll, chain cookie and cookie storm on 3% (needs 100k earned), and building special on 25% (needs 10+ buildings). There is an 80% chance to strip the previous effect from the pool, so the same event rarely fires twice in a row. Source: main.js lines 5669-5700.

Cookie Clicker payloads, the template for bounded events. Lucky = min(15% of bank, 15 min of CpS) + 13. Ruin = min(5% of bank, 10 min of CpS) + 13, capped at the bank. Clot = x0.5 CpS for 66 s. Frenzy = x7 for 77 s. Click frenzy = x777 clicks for 13 s. The min-of-two bound means a loss can never wipe the player. Source: main.js lines 5775-5815.

Clicker Heroes Primal Bosses: 25% chance on each boss zone from 100 (falls 0.02 every 500 zones). Zones 110, 120 and 130 are guaranteed, which gives players a known target for the first ascension. Source: https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Formulas and https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Ascension.

Universal Paperclips rescue events. Computing unlocks early if the player has no wire, no clips and too little money for wire. 'Beg for More Wire' (1 Trust) appears in the same dead state. Source: https://www.decisionproblem.com/paperclips/main.js line 3473 and projects.js line 35.
Universal Paperclips milestone events: Trust arrives at Fibonacci x 1000 clips (3000, 5000, 8000, 13000, ...). These are deterministic milestones, not random ones. Source: main.js lines 3374-3383.
Cookie Clicker changelog: 'buffs no longer affect offline CpS'. Timed event buffs are kept out of offline catch-up. Source: main.js line 1681.
pacing: First purchase arrives within seconds in every reference game. Cookie Clicker: Cursor costs 15 cookies, so 15 clicks (main.js line 8979). AdVenture Capitalist: the first Lemonade Stand is free and the second costs $4, about 4 cycles of 0.6 s. Kittens Game: field costs 10 catnip. Antimatter Dimensions: D1 costs 10 AM. Clicker Heroes: Treebeast costs 50 gold. Universal Paperclips: the AutoClipper costs $5.

First automation comes within the first minutes. Cookie Clicker: the Cursor is the first purchase and auto-clicks every 10 s. Paperclips: the AutoClipper at $5. AdVenture Capitalist: the Lemonade manager costs $1,000, about 600 s of a single stand's base 1.67/s; buying more stands brings it sooner. My estimate is a few minutes, unconfirmed by any source. Sources: https://adventure-capitalist.fandom.com/wiki/Managers and https://www.decisionproblem.com/paperclips/globals.js.

Tier payback grows geometrically. AdVenture Capitalist base payback by tier: 2.2, 3, 8, 24, 48, 192, 768, 3072, 12288, 32056 s, so x2 to x4 a tier. Cookie Clicker: Cursor 150 s, then Grandma onward 100, 138, 255, 500, 1000, 2564, 7500, 19615 s, so x1.4 to x2.9 a tier. Computed from the cited tables.

Cost ratio guide (computed). 1.07 doubles every 10.2 buys and is x5.4 at 25, x29 at 50. 1.10 doubles every 7.3 and is x10.8 at 25. 1.12 doubles every 6.1 and is x17 at 25. 1.15 doubles every 5.0 and is x33 at 25, x1080 at 50. 1.25 doubles every 3.1 and is x265 at 25. AdVenture Capitalist uses 1.15 on cheap tiers down to 1.07 on expensive ones. Cookie Clicker uses 1.15 everywhere. Kittens uses 1.15 by default, 1.12 for food and 1.25 to 2.5 for capacity buildings. Clicker Heroes uses 1.07, or 1.22 for Ace Scouts.

Milestone bumps break the exponential grind. AdVenture Capitalist halves cycle time at 25/50/100/200/300/400 owned. Antimatter Dimensions gives x2 per 10 bought. Clicker Heroes gives x4 per 25 levels from level 200. Pecorella: multipliers give 'bumps and local victories' (GDC 2016 slide 16).

First prestige thresholds. Cookie Clicker: level 1 at 1e12 cookies all-time, with the wiki advising a first ascension at 365 chips (about 4.9e19 cookies). AdVenture Capitalist: first angel at about $4.44e10 lifetime. Clicker Heroes: unlock at Amenhotep level 150, ascend at zone 130 or later. Antimatter Dimensions: 1.79e308 AM. Realm Grinder: 1e12 max coins. Egg, Inc.: 1e6 run earnings. Wall-clock times for these first prestiges are unconfirmed: I found no source giving minutes or hours.

Pecorella's prestige timing rule: players reset when they would gain +50% to +200% prestige currency. Take a log or fractional exponent to slow growth. Make sure players reach a valuable prestige point regularly. Make the start of the next run quick, because the regained power is the reward. Cycles that grow slower need a meta prestige. Source: https://media.gdcvault.com/gdceurope2016/presentations/Pecorella_Anthony_Quest%20for%20Progress.pdf.

GridInc blog (search snippet only, not fetched): prestige makes sense when progress slows to 10-20% of peak speed, and each milestone should take roughly the same relative time. https://gridinc.co.za/blog/idle-games-best-practices
Active skill cadence: Pecorella says active skills typically have cooldowns of 5 minutes to a few hours (GDC 2016 slide 18). Cookie Clicker's golden cookies arrive about every 7.4 min.

Offline caps: Egg, Inc. caps offline earning at 2 h, and Pecorella calls this 'a mistake' that made him churn (GDC 2016 slide 55). AdVenture Capitalist managers run fully offline. Cookie Clicker gives 5% of CpS for 1 h and 0.5% after that, and only through a prestige perk.
prestige: Square root, AdVenture Capitalist: angels = 150*sqrt(L/1e15), minus angels already claimed, +2% each, additive. Doubling needs x4 lifetime. A reset at the same point still pays a little. Angels can be sacrificed for upgrades at the loss of their bonus. https://adventure-capitalist.fandom.com/wiki/Angel_Investors

Cube root, Cookie Clicker: prestige = (allTimeCookies/1e12)^(1/3), +1% CpS per level, unlocked step by step through heavenly upgrades. Doubling needs x8 lifetime. https://orteil.dashnet.org/cookieclicker/main.js lines 4185-4194 and 5175

Triangular inverse, Realm Grinder and Kittens karma: p = (sqrt(1 + 8c/s) - 1)/2. Doubling needs x3.0 (p 1 to 2), x3.67 (5 to 10) and tends to x4. Realm Grinder uses MAX coins in a run, so resetting at the same point pays nothing. https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/the-math-of-idle-games-part-iii and https://github.com/nuclear-unicorn/kittensgame/blob/master/js/game.js
Steep root, Egg, Inc.: delta_p = (c_R/1e6)^0.14. Doubling needs about x141. Forces long runs. Same Part III source.

Log-like, Clicker Heroes: 1 soul per 2000 hero levels, plus primal bosses floor(((z-80)/25)^1.3); +10% DPS per soul. Because levels track the log of gold, souls grow like a log of currency. https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Hero_Souls
Extreme root for nested layers, Antimatter Dimensions: IP = 10^(floor(log10 AM)/308 - 0.75); EP about 0.324*IP^(1/440.65). https://antimatter-dimensions.fandom.com/wiki/Break_Infinity

Reset-gain to lifetime-growth map (computed). To gain x1.5 / x2 / x3 prestige: sqrt needs lifetime x2.25 / x4 / x9; cube root needs x3.4 / x8 / x27. Under Pecorella's +50% to +200% rule, sqrt gives shorter, more frequent runs than cube root.

Bonus per prestige unit in shipped games: +1% (Cookie Clicker), +2% additive (AdVenture Capitalist), +10% (Clicker Heroes). Prestige currency should grow 'at a slower order of magnitude than primary currency' (Pecorella, GDC 2016 slide 20).

toKin today: core/distill.ts pays Logits = floor(distillK*sqrt(lifetimeTokens/distillT0)) - logitsEarned, with distillK = 8 and distillT0 = 2000 (content/era1.json). This is the AdVenture Capitalist shape with the subtract-earned rule. It needs a T0 retune for the new economy (see lessons).
surveys.activeVsIdle: Shipped games give active play an edge of roughly x1.5 to x3 over idle, and they do it through attention windows, not through a flat clicking requirement. Cookie Clicker: golden cookies spawn about every 7.4 min, last 13 s and are half Frenzy (x7 for 77 s), Lucky (min(15% bank, 15 min CpS)) and so on. If half of the cookies are Frenzy, the average multiplier is about 1 + 6*0.5*77/446, roughly x1.5, before Lucky and click effects; this is my estimate. Each mouse upgrade adds +1% of CpS per click. Offline play pays only 5% of CpS (0.5% after 1 h), and only through a prestige perk. Clicker Heroes splits the styles into separate prestige upgrades. Idle bonuses (Siyalatas DPS, Libertas +25% gold per level) apply after 60 s without a click and cancel after 2 clicks in 5 min. Active Juggernaut stacks need a click at least every 280 s and decay 5%/s once the player stops (https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Libertas,_Ancient_of_Freedom, https://clickerheroes.fandom.com/wiki/Juggernaut,_Ancient_of_Momentum). AdVenture Capitalist's managers make idle play fully viable offline. Egg, Inc.'s 2 h offline cap was called a churn-causing mistake by Pecorella (GDC 2016). Pecorella's active skills, with 5 min to multi-hour cooldowns, let players 'burst income or get over a hump'. Input policing: Cookie Clicker ignores clicks under 20 ms apart, holds keyboard-activated clicks to 3/s and flags anything over 15/s as an autoclicker (main.js lines 4988-4999). For toKin the edge is already structural. Under D16, at 2x demand an active player who queues gets 100% of the machine and an idle player gets 50%. At 1.25x the split is 100% against 80%. The D17 scheduler node then lets idle players earn most of that back, the way Clicker Heroes sells idle and active ancients separately. toKin's current offline cap is 7200 s (2 h), or 8 h after Night Shift (core/offline.ts, content/era1.json): the same 2 h figure Pecorella criticised.
lessonsForToKin: Typing ladder, cost ratio: presses per level = C0*(r/2)^L, so r must be above 2 or the ladder never slows (D3 already notes this). Recommend C0 = 10 and r = 3 as the placeholder (dev panel range 2.5 to 4). That puts the first purchase at 10 presses, about 2 s, like Cookie Clicker's 15-click Cursor and AdVenture Capitalist's $4 second stand. Eight levels (256 tokens per press) take 493 presses, about 1.6 min at 5 presses/s. r = 3.5 takes 3.9 min and r = 4 takes 8.5 min. Keep the hands-only phase at 2 to 5 minutes, because every reference game automates within the first minutes. Cookie Clicker's own finger track steps x5 then x20 per doubling, which is steeper but runs alongside idle income; toKin's ladder is the only income at that point, so it should be gentler.

Typing ladder, cap and first net (D19): put the cap at level 7 or 8 (128 to 256 tokens per press) on the first computer. Price the first net's design plus code at about 60 to 120 s of pressing at the cap (with 256 tokens/press at 5/s, about 75k to 150k tokens). Make training a short first time-gate of 30 to 60 s at its fixed MIPS demand. The player then gets automation inside 5 minutes, matching AdVenture Capitalist's managers and Paperclips' AutoClipper.

Typing ladder, key input (D22): drop KeyboardEvent.repeat events (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/KeyboardEvent/repeat), or a held key earns tokens at the OS repeat rate. Also cap counted presses, for example at 12 to 15 per second. Cookie Clicker ignores clicks under 20 ms apart, holds keyboard-activated clicks to 3/s and flags anything over 15/s. The on-screen button in the Claude Code pane should get the same cap.

Copy costs (D5): use copyCost_k = base * r^k with r = 1.12 as the placeholder (panel range 1.07 to 1.15). Copies are also limited by MIPS (D16) and by dedup, so the full 1.15 would stack three brakes. 1.12 doubles every 6.1 copies and reaches x17 by copy 25; 1.15 would reach x33. Add ownership milestones at 10, 25 and 50 copies, for example halving MIPS per copy or doubling output. AdVenture Capitalist halves cycle time at 25/50/100, Antimatter Dimensions gives x2 per 10 and Clicker Heroes x4 per 25 levels. They give 'bumps and local victories' against the exponent.

Dedup event (D5): derive it from birthday math instead of a timer. Each copy draws from S distinct outputs, where S is seed diversity. Unique output = S*(1 - (1 - 1/S)^k), and P(any repeat) ~ 1 - e^(-k(k-1)/(2S)). With S = 50, 10 copies already have a 59% chance of a repeat at 91% unique, and 50 copies are 64% unique. Fire the dedup event the first time unique/k drops below a threshold such as 90%. Show effective copies as k*unique%. Dedup spend raises S. The data cleaning node (D9) cuts dedup cost. Later, scraped data and book scanning (brainstorm) raise S for good. The bad synthetic data event can cut S or a quality multiplier, so bad data gets the same kind of hit as repeats.

Gig money (D6): build gigs as an AdVenture Capitalist-style tier table. Each new gig tier asks about x10 to x12 more input (tokens or prose), lasts about x2 then x4 longer (AdVenture Capitalist cycles: 0.6, 3, 6, 12, 24, 96, 384 s ...), and has a payback about x2 to x4 longer than the tier below. Make deadlines generous, at least 2x the expected time at the current rate. A failed gig should cost only the time spent, never money or tokens. Add a Paperclips-style rescue: if the player has no money, no affordable gig and no income, offer a guaranteed small gig. That covers D23's never soft-lock rule.

Hardware compute (D7, D11, D15): use chip generations as tiers that each add about x2 to x4 MIPS, as real CPUs did: 8080 0.29 (1974), Z80 0.58 (1976), 68000 1.4 (1979), 286 1.28 (1982), 386DX 2.15 (1985), 486DX 8.7 (1989), Pentium 188 (1994) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instructions_per_second). That also matches the x2 to x4 payback step of AdVenture Capitalist tiers. A garage start near 0.1 to 0.5 MIPS fits the loose 19xx setting. Repeat buys of the same item (more cores, more machines) should use a low ratio of 1.07 to 1.10, like AdVenture Capitalist's expensive tiers and the Kittens observatory. Paperclips warns that a speed against capacity split (processors against memory) can stall a run if the player over-buys one side. Since D15 RAM caps net size, let the player sell hardware back (Cookie Clicker refunds 25%) or warn before a buy that leaves the machine unable to load the next net.

Oversubscription (D16) numbers to show in the UI: machine throughput = c/d, so 1.25x demand does 80% of the work, 1.5x 67%, 2x 50%, 3x 33%. Per-job speed is the square of that: 64%, 44%, 25%, 11%. This is toKin's version of an active bonus. Active queueing holds 100%, and the D17 scheduler node closes the gap for idle players, as Clicker Heroes sells idle and active ancients separately.

Pipelines (D8): treat specialised tokens as Pecorella's 'primary exchange currency', a currency between raw output and its use that lets the designer 'gate or buff conversion at certain points'. Model each converter as (input ratio, MIPS demand, output multiplier). Upgrade the output multiplier, as Kittens does with amt*(1+craftRatio), and keep input ratios fixed so the numbers stay readable. Kittens chains run 175 furs to parchment, 25 parchment plus 400 culture to manuscript, 55 manuscripts plus 9000 science to compendium, and 25 compendia plus 25000 science to blueprint. Because typed tokens exist only in flight, give each pipeline a buffer cap. Borrow Paperclips' overflow rule (full ops spill into Creativity) so a pipeline that backs up while idle feeds a small side resource instead of wasting time.

Publishing events (D20): use Cookie Clicker's hazard. Once minTime has passed, each tick has chance ((t - min)/(max - min))^5. With min 5 and max 15 min the mean is 7.4 min and 80% of events fall in 6.8 to 8.0 min, so events feel random but come on a beat. Keep Cookie Clicker's 80% rule against repeating the last event. Bound every cost like the wrath cookie 'Ruin', min(5% of bank, 10 min of production) + 13. For 'market catches up', cut gig pay by about 3% with a floor at about 70% of base and slow recovery. For 'rival adopts your method', move that paper's edge a fixed share, for example 25% of what remains, back toward x1. Give Citations positive golden-cookie events too, such as a press interview paying min(15% of bank, 15 min of production) as Lucky does. Keep timed buffs out of offline catch-up, which Cookie Clicker changed to do.

Distill (D23), shape and tuning: keep the square root with the subtract-earned rule that core/distill.ts already uses. It is AdVenture Capitalist's 150*sqrt(L/1e15) shape, so any reset after growth pays something and doubling needs x4 lifetime tokens. Retune distillT0 for the new economy. With K = 8 and T0 = 2000, the r = 3 typing ladder alone (32,800 tokens spent) would pay about 32 Logits before the first net exists. Set T0 = L1*(K/n1)^2, where L1 is lifetime tokens a short while after the first AI paper and n1 is the target first payout of about 3 to 10 Logits. Under Pecorella's +50% to +200% rule, sqrt players will Distill each time lifetime grows x2.25 to x9. Cube root (Cookie Clicker) would ask x3.4 to x27; save it for a later meta layer.

Distill (D23), no soft-lock and a fast restart: keep the logits >= 1 gate (canDistill), so a Distill can never pay zero, unlike Realm Grinder's max-coins form. Make sure the next run is visibly faster at the start. Pecorella: 'Will their progress through the early part be quick?' Nonstop Knight speeds through early content after a prestige. Do this by keeping typing ladder levels, or by auto-buying them, and by starting the first net cheaper. If Logits can be spent, as with AdVenture Capitalist angels, show the multiplier lost before the player confirms.

Active against idle: aim for active play paying about x1.5 to x3 over idle, the range Cookie Clicker reaches through golden cookies (my estimate is about x1.5 from Frenzy alone). Don't let active pay x10, or idle play stops being a real choice. Sources of the edge: manual queueing against the D16 penalty, golden-cookie-style publishing and Citation events that need a click within about 13 s, and pipeline tending (D8). Pecorella calls Egg, Inc.'s 2 h offline cap a mistake, yet toKin's offlineCapSeconds is 7200. Raise it to at least 8 to 12 h for everyone, and simulate offline time at the idle rate, which already carries the oversubscription penalty.

Polynomial against exponential across the whole economy: keep costs exponential and production polynomial everywhere except the typing ladder, which doubles. That makes the ladder exponential on both sides, so its slowdown rests entirely on r/2 and it needs the hard cap (D19). Clicker Heroes shows the default decay: DPS/cost at level 199 is 0.03% of level 1 without milestones. Later 'nets that design nets' should use the derivative-chain model (x^n/n!), which grows polynomially and only approaches exponential as tiers are added.

Dev panel (Q5): expose these knobs. Ladder C0, r and cap level. Copy base and ratio. Milestone counts and multipliers. Seed space S and dedup threshold. Gig tier cost step, time step and deadline multiplier. Hardware tier MIPS step and repeat-buy ratio. Oversubscription exponent (default 2). Event minTime, maxTime and hazard exponent (default 5, 15 and 5). Event loss caps (bank % and minutes of production). Distill K, T0 and root exponent (default 0.5). Offline cap and offline rate. Every value above is a placeholder taken from a shipped game or my own estimate, for the balance bot to tune.

gaps: D17 first stage (the priority list decides which jobs slow down most) has no formula or param. Un-queued jobs all run at the same (C/D)^2, so the priority list does nothing until the player queues by hand or owns the Scheduler. A per-priority slowdown weighting needs a param (e.g. compute.priorityWeight).
D17 Scheduler scope: the decision says it auto-queues 'the lowest jobs'. The recommendation treats it as a full hand-queue equivalent, and no param sets which or how many jobs it queues.

D8 routing: no rule or param says where converter output goes when no consumer is active (buffer size, backpressure or waste). Paper and node costs are written as amounts (20k prose, 8k research) with no in-flight model.

D8 consumers: gigs and net design are named as places pipelines feed, but gig.tokens are raw at every tier and net.designCost is raw at every tier. Only net code (from MLP on), papers and research use specialised tokens.
D8: the Transformer as the universal converter has no curve or params. It appears only as a 'later era' depth 7 research node.
D8: the active premium from pipeline management (keeping pipelines optimal) has no mechanic or param beyond MIPS allocation, and the pacing sim leaves it out.
D9 Scale lever (fixed model sizes, where more parameters need more data tokens and compute) has no curve. Training needs no data tokens, and each architecture has one size.
D10 grants (Citations unlock grants) have no curve or param. Better clients are covered by gig.citeGate; hires are explicitly later.

D10 edge for non-architecture results: research.archEdge exists only for architectures. Papers on techniques or skills (Backprop, Touch typing, Write it up) have no edge for 'a rival adopts your method' to fade.
D23: no rule defines a 'paper on AI'. Depth 1 results include Touch typing and Write it up, so it is unclear which paper starts distill.unlockDelay.
D15 'more cores' has no distinct item or param. The tiers are co-processor, faster CPU, extra machine, minicomputer and mainframe time.

D19 and D3: the cap on later machines defaults to never lifting (ladder.capPerHardwareTier = 0). The decision only fixes the cap on the first machine, so behaviour after hardware upgrades is an unconfirmed choice.
Gig unlock persistence: nothing says whether a gig tier stays unlocked after token income drops below gig.unlockSlack x tokens/deadline. This matters for the no-soft-lock rule (see contradictions).
Brainstorm (not yet decided, so optional): manual scraping has no MIPS demand or job param. Agentic-net scraping and book or manuscript scanning are mentioned in the formula text but have no params.
contradictions: D3 (one manual upgrade track, 'one track for now') vs a second set of press upgrades: press-skill research nodes (Touch typing, Shorthand, Dictation, each adding press.netShare 2% of net output per press), the Flow inspiration (x7 press tokens), ladder.capPerHardwareTier, and the Muscle memory Distill node. The user should sign off on these extra press-upgrade paths.

D5 ('any overlap is hand-waved' until the 'copies start to repeat' event) vs the birthday-math penalty u(n) = S(1 - (1 - 1/S)^n), which cuts output from copy 2 on. At S=16 the unique share is 0.97, 0.94 and 0.91 at 2, 3 and 4 copies, so 4 copies already lose 9% before the event fires at copy 5. Apply the penalty only after the event, or confirm with the user.
D8 (pipelines feed gigs and net design) vs gigs and net design paid in raw tokens at every tier. Only net code, papers and research take specialised tokens.

D8 (the pool holds raw tokens; specialised tokens exist only inside pipelines) vs costs written as stocks (paper 20k prose, research node 8k research, data tokens 'fed' to seed space). With no in-flight or routing model, an implementer will likely add separate pools, against D8.

D17 (before the Scheduler, the priority list decides which jobs slow down most) vs the oversubscription curve, where every un-queued job slows equally at (C/D)^compute.oversubExponent. Priorities have no effect before queuing.

D22 (any key press on the keyboard counts as a press) vs press.maxCounted = 15/s, which drops real presses above 15/s. Filtering KeyboardEvent.repeat is arguably fine because a held key is not a new press, but the rate cap needs the user's confirmation.
D10 (publishing makes 'the edge from that research' fade) vs an edge defined only for architectures (research.archEdge). For any other published result the rival event changes nothing.

Never-soft-lock ground rule (and D23) vs the gig unlock rule: tier 1 unlocks only when token income >= 2 x 8,000/60 = 267 T/s. A player at the ladder cap who stops pressing earns at most 240 T/s from 4 Perceptron copies on 1 MIPS. A 5th copy drops output to about 192 T/s under D16. One press per second at L8 adds 256 T/s, which on its own is also below 267. The soft-lock audit says tier 1 'is always on the board after the cap', which contradicts the rule. Without gigs there is no money for the $100 RAM upgrade the MLP needs (8 KB) or for hardware. Fix: make tier 1 unconditional at the cap, or make unlocks permanent once reached.

Internal, touching D2: the prestige section says a reset restores 'hand presses (1 token per press)', but press income is 2^L x LogitMult, which is 1.75 tokens per press at run 2's start with 15 Logits. Either exempt presses from LogitMult or reword the claim.
