issues: Verified as claimed: ladder 32,800 tokens or 493 presses (82 s at 6/s, 164 s at 3/s, 246 s at 2/s); copy prices; dedup events at copies 5, 8, 15, 29, 56, 111, 221; the D16 table; gig unlock incomes and money ceilings; dollars per MIPS; training times; event timers (pub mean 4.00 min, p10 3.48, p90 4.48; Inspiration mean 7.57 min, 6.65 to 8.42). The opening hits its targets: L1 1 s/4 s, cap 84/247, training start 133/394, net trained 178/439, first hardware 166 (target 165), converters 458 (476).
Typo: 5e8 lifetime tokens pay 61 Logits, not 63 (15 x sqrt(16.7) = 61.2).
The first net trained at 178 s leaves only 2 s under the <180 s target. Anything slower than 6 presses/s fails it.

Distill payout is badly calibrated. At unlock, sensible strategies have 4.8M to 10.5M run tokens (median), not the 3.3e7 to 3.5e7 the rec claims. With t0 = 3e7 that pays 5 to 8 Logits instead of 15. At the real payout, run 2 is only 1.25x to 1.5x faster, short of the 2x target. At a forced 15 Logits, active reaches 2.40x.

Distill unlocks too early for an active player who rushes the paper. Researching MLP and then Write it up gives the first paper at 1087 s and Distill at 1387 s (23 min). That is under the 1800-2700 s window and the 1970 s target, and pays 6 Logits. The paper path is limited only by converters: 16k research plus 20k prose. Lifetime at unlock varies 2x to 10x with research order.

Soft wall at gig tier 1. Its gate of 267 T/s is above the most the basic machine's nets can earn: 4 Perceptron copies give 218 T/s after the repeat loss u(4) = 3.64, or 262 T/s at 4 Logits. Only presses get past it.

Strict idle has a dead zone after the first net. Income falls from 512 T/s (pressing) to 60 T/s at 439 s and stays under 650 T/s until about 2100 s. Converters unlock at 2334 s against an 1800 s target.

Idle money is capped by the gig board. Three offers per tier per check-in pay $36 (tier 1) or $252 (tiers 1 and 2) every 10 min, about 0.42 $/s at most. The active ceiling is 3 $/s, so idle gets about 7x less money. The Faster CPU at $702 then takes many check-ins. Strict idle opens tier 2 (1422 T/s) only after its MLP is trained. With dedup.bonus at 1.25, strict idle sat at 1187 T/s from 4200 s to 9600 s with MIPS full.

Idle pacing is bound by how many decisions happen in a row. Every converter, research node and paper needs a check-in, so idle run-2 speedup is only 1.2x to 1.7x even at 15 Logits, against 2.4x for active. Results move in 10-min steps.

Active-to-idle time to Distill unlock is 3.7x for strict idle (above the 1.5x-3x target), 2.9x for casual idle and 2.2x for 5-min check-ins. Early milestones differ by 3x to 7x: the copies-repeat event comes at 1081-1321 s idle against a 639 s target.

Dedup compounds too hard. x1.5 per dedup reaches x5.06 by copy 29, which outweighs the x2 output-per-MIPS step between tiers. A Perceptron with 4 dedups earns 1215 T/s per MIPS. A fresh MLP earns 600 including its 25% edge, so MLP copies queue behind old Perceptrons until MLP reaches copy 8. Dedup is also almost free: 18.9k tokens for x1.5 at copy 5.

The code converter is dead content. Price in code tokens times conv.codeRatio equals the raw price, so a code converter never saves raw tokens. It costs 100k tokens and 0.5 MIPS and caps code at 100/s. In the sim, the MLP trained 300 s later with one (1360 s against 1060 s).

Taking every gig offer is a trap. Tiers 1 and 2 together ask 2,533 T/s, but active income at the cap is 1,536 T/s. A bot that took every offer and filled it over time kept copies at 1 and built no converters in 4 h. The rec's active profile, 'catches every gig offer', does not work as written.
Converters draw raw tokens before any purchase. If their input is at or above income, the pool stays at 0. The bot had to cap converters at 60% of income and pause them while saving.
Presses still give 34% of active income at 10 min and 21% at 20 min, settling near 27% once the three press nodes are owned. The first Perceptron's 60 T/s is 4% of capped active typing.

Inspiration is confirmed at about +20% to +30% speed: 1e8 run tokens at 2700-3000 s instead of 3300 s, and 1e9 at 4500-5100 s instead of 6000 s, with Distill unlock unchanged. Ratios measured at a fixed time reach 2x to 25x by 90 min because tier unlocks amplify any lead. Judge the active premium by time-to-milestone, not by output at a fixed time.

Mid-game money stalls with default params. Active MIPS sits at 24.2 from about 2900 s to 5300 s while money is saved for 512 KB RAM ($72.9k, needed for Attention). The tier 1-4 money ceiling is about 51 $/s, and tier 4 also needs 25 Citations. This is partly the bot's priority order.

conv.unlockLifetime says 'lifetime tokens', but core/distill.ts counts lifetimeTokens across every run. If converters read that number, they are open from t=0 in run 2. The sim used tokens from the current run only.

With the suggested changes, active reaches the third hardware tier at 48 min instead of 89 min and has 137 MIPS at 60 min instead of 24. Watch pacing after Distill. If the mid-game feels fast, use gig.unlockSlack 1.75.

Sim limits: 1 s ticks; greedy bot with a fixed research order (MLP, Write it up, Backprop and so on); no offline time, data or GPUs; the market and rival events are modelled. The bot saves for net stages and the first converter of each kind. The idle bot never pauses jobs and buys copies only into free MIPS.
softLockRisks: Gig tier 1 locks out a player who never presses if gates are checked live instead of staying open once reached. Proven: strict idle stayed at 218 T/s with 4 copies and $48 for 6 h, with no hardware, no paper and no Distill. Make gates sticky and drop the income gate on tier 1.

Warm start in run 2 skips the ladder cap, which is the only trigger for the gig board (D19). Proven: strict idle in run 2 with 0, 2 or 4 Logits never opened tier 1 and never published in 6 h. Its 4 copies earned 218-262 T/s, under the 267 T/s gate. 6+ Logits got through, and pressing always escapes. Fix: the board also opens when the first net runs.

'Code is paid only in code tokens once a code converter exists': if that converter is paused, starved or sold, MLP and later code can no longer be paid in raw tokens. Always accept raw tokens, at a markup.

Converters whose input is at or above income drain the pool to 0 every tick, so nothing else is ever affordable. Pausing escapes it, but an idle player may not notice. Add a pipeline budget, such as a max share of raw income.
Accepted gigs draw from the pool before anything else, so over-accepting starves copies and nets. The 50% refund bounds the loss.

Checked and safe: a player who never takes a gig still publishes at 1248 s and unlocks Distill at 1548 s, though the MLP needs RAM that costs money. Naive oversubscription only delays Distill, to 8580 s. Every D16 speed stays above 0. Overclock crash losses are capped. With the suggested changes, both lockout probes pass: strict idle with live gates reaches Distill at 5100 s, and run 2 with 0-8 Logits opens tier 1 at 45 s and publishes by 3000-4200 s.

suggestedChanges.why: New rule: tier 1 opens with the board and has no income gate. Its 267 T/s gate is above the basic machine's 218 T/s net output and causes both lockouts. Keep every tier gate sticky once reached.
New rule: the gig board opens at the ladder cap or when the first net runs, whichever comes first. Warm start skips the cap. Fixes the run-2 idle lockout.
Opens tier 2 at 1067 T/s instead of 1422, so strict idle no longer lives on $12 tier-1 gigs. Use 1.75 if the active mid-game gets too fast.
An idle player who checks in every 10 min collects only boardSize offers per tier, about 7x less money than active. 8 roughly halves that gap. Active is unaffected.
Together with the paper cost, this puts a paper-rushing active Distill unlock at 1810 s (window 1800-2700, target 1970) instead of 1387, and pane at 2176.
The first paper alone gated Distill at 23 min with a 6-Logit payout. This also gives the prose pipeline more weight.
Run tokens at unlock are 8M to 17M under the suggested set, not 3e7. This pays 12 to 18 Logits at unlock across strategies and gives active and pane 2.0x to 2.25x run-2 speedup at the real payout.
x1.5 compounds to x5.06 by copy 29, so old nets out-earn the next tier per MIPS. 1.3 gives x2.86 after 4 dedups. Use 1.25 (x2.44) if a net with 4 dedups should stay below a fresh next tier.
Offsets the lower dedup bonus and softens the idle income cliff at the first net. 4 copies make about 327 T/s, above the old tier-1 gate.
New param: raw tokens pay MLP and later code at 2x. A code converter then halves the raw cost. Today it never saves anything and only adds cost, MIPS and a throughput cap.
